items.title: ProofPatch: Reviewing Lean Statements and Keeping the Reviews Valid as Formalizations Evolve
items.summary: The kernel of the Lean proof assistant checks that a proof establishes its statement. Whether the statement says what was intended is left to human reviewers. This is the old problem of validating a specification, and it grows more pressing as language models write formal statements in bulk and agents edit formal developments continuously. We present ProofPatch, a tool that helps reviewers judge Lean statements and keeps their judgments valid while the development changes. A reviewer can ask the kernel targeted…

items.title: Optimal Strategies to Contain and Prevent the Spread of Diseases in Group-structured Populations
items.summary: The strength and speed of an epidemic process in a multiplex network is affected by how modular the networks in each layer are. However, it is not obvious how the dynamics of the spreading process change when the group structure and membership varies between layers. In this work, we demonstrate that restructuring the organization of groups within a population can be used as an effective strategy to decrease the severity of an epidemic. Specifically, we show that when group structures are sufficiently correlated…

items.title: Same Function, Different Mechanism: Implementation-Local Geometry Beyond Accuracy
items.summary: Two models can make exactly the same predictions yet respond differently when their implementations are perturbed. A lookup table can change one case independently; a shared rule couples changes across cases. We compare these mechanisms through an implementation chart: a specified local family of logit perturbations around a fixed predictive distribution. Our main result counts the independent prediction changes allowed by exact finite-group sharing: the active dimension is the number of input-output orbits minus…

items.title: Floquet engineering of quantum relaxation
items.summary: Dynamical decoupling suppresses decoherence by averaging selected interactions between a quantum system and its environment. Here, we extend this notion through a general Floquet formalism that maps periodic control onto relaxation and dephasing channels. Environmental fluctuations are decomposed into Floquet components that sample the noise spectrum at distinct frequencies, with coupling strengths determined by control-induced Floquet coefficients. We experimentally investigate this approach using a single…

items.title: Heavy quark thermalization using phonon-heavy quark EFT
items.summary: The description of heavy quarks inside the QGP medium, especially at low momenta, remains challenging from first principles, due to large coupling strength and gluon occupation numbers. An alternative way to formulate a description in terms of perturbative degrees of freedom is the interaction of the heavy quarks with the collective excitations of the medium in the form of phonons. This description is derived as an effective field theory (EFT) and therefore allows for a natural occurring power counting of the…

items.title: Gromov-Witten theory of the local model of the standard flop
items.summary: We conjecture that the generating series of equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants of the local Calabi-Yau $(2n-1)$-fold $\operatorname{Tot} \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{n-1}} (-1)^{\oplus n}$ at fixed genus can be presented as a linear combination of polylogarithms, generalising a well-known property of the resolved conifold. We prove this conjecture for two specialisations of the equivariant parameters. In the first, the parameters are specialised to roots of unity and the proof proceeds via Givental-Teleman…

items.title: $a$-contraction applied to the time-asymptotic stability of weak shocks for a general 1-D viscous system
items.summary: The method of $a$-contraction with shifts builds on the relative entropy method of Dafermos and DiPerna and allows both viscous shocks and rarefaction waves to be studied directly at the level of the solution. This unified framework led to the resolution of Matsumura's long-standing conjecture on the time-asymptotic stability of a viscous shock in composition with a rarefaction. Kang, Vasseur, and Wang established this stability for the one-dimensional compressible barotropic Navier-Stokes system. Their result…

items.title: Modular proof analysis and cut elimination for the Reflection Calculi $\mathsfRC_1$ and $\mathsfQRC_1$
items.summary: The reflection calculus with one modality is denoted by $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and its quantified generalization is known as $\mathsf{QRC}_1$. These decidable calculi are of interest since they generate the strictly positive fragments of the (quantified) provability logic for theories like Peano Arithmetic and Heyting Arithmetic. We introduce analytic cut-free calculi ${\mathrm{GRC1}}$ and ${\mathrm{GQRC1}}$ for $\mathsf{RC}_1$ and $\mathsf{QRC}_1$ respectively. The new calculi derive sequents of the form…

items.title: Entanglement for elliptic curve group orders
items.summary: For an elliptic curve $E$ defined over a number field $K$ and $\mathfrak{p}$ a prime of good reduction of $E/K$, we let $n_\mathfrak{p}=\#E(k_\mathfrak{p})$ be the order of the group of points over the residue class field $k_\mathfrak{p}$. Divisibility of $n_\mathfrak{p}$ by a prime $\ell$ depends on the splitting behavior of $\mathfrak{p}$ in the $\ell$-division field $K(E[\ell](\bar{K}))$ of $E$ and, generically, divisibility of $n_\mathfrak{p}$ by different primes $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ are `independent events'…

items.title: A model-based adaptive sampling framework for infectious disease surveillance
items.summary: Longitudinal surveillance must choose each round's sampling design before the next observations arrive. Fixed sample-size rules treat each round as an isolated cross-sectional survey and ignore the evolving uncertainty in the epidemic process, which changes as transmission, vaccination, interventions, variants, and behavior change. We present a model-based adaptive sampling framework for choosing the next-round design. A state-space model represents the epidemic process and maps latent states to surveillance…

items.title: A Domain Driven Design Based Reference Architecture for IoT Systems Engineering
items.summary: The Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm continues to gain significant traction across diverse do-mains, primarily driven by its transformative and socio-economic benefits. However, engineering robust IoT systems remains a formidable challenge, largely due to the inherent dynamism, volatility, and uncertainty of their operational environments. To mitigate this architectural complexity, microservices have emerged as a viable alternative to traditional, rigid monolithic frameworks, offering a scalable mechanism to…

items.title: Daemon sub Ponte: The Cost of a Second Black Hole (A Scholium on an ER=EPR Thought Experiment)
items.summary: A thought experiment in the ER=EPR and related literature involves collecting the Hawking radiation of an old black hole, then collapsing it into a second, entangled black hole. In this short note, we examine the resources required by this idealized conversion. More specifically, we are interested in answering the question: how much external energy is needed to form the second black hole? Assuming a semiclassical bound on the information capacity of the newly formed black hole, we derive a conditional lower bound…

items.title: All-to-All Connectivity in Superconducting Qubits via Metamaterial-Mediated Interactions
items.summary: We show that encoding superconducting qubits as dual-rail or spin-locked transmons lets a metamaterial waveguide couple them all-to-all while suppressing the spurious entanglement that burdens shared-mode architectures, a step toward the non-local connectivity that quantum low-density parity-check codes require. In a bare-transmon architecture, the dispersive coupling between each populated mode and every idle qubit attached to it entangles spectators with the gate, and cancelling it by dynamical decoupling…

items.title: Physics-Informed Functional Tucker Method with RKHS Factors for Sparse Spatiotemporal Reconstruction
items.summary: Reconstructing physical dynamics from fixed sparse sensors and missing frames is a fundamental challenge in scientific research. Sparsity leaves large regions of the field unconstrained, making the inverse problem ill-posed: a model may fit the observed sensors while producing inaccurate off-sensor structures or unreliable predictions between support frames. To this end, we propose PhysFTM---a physics-informed functional Tucker model that parameterizes the Tucker mode factors in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces…

items.title: EMG-Hybrid: A Dual-Engine Elite Memory--Guided Adaptive Optimization Framework for High-Dimensional Feature Selection
items.summary: Feature selection in ultra-high-dimensional, noisy datasets remains a critical challenge due to exponential search space growth, where conventional binary metaheuristics often suffer from premature convergence. To address this, EMG-Hybrid is introduced as a novel three-level hierarchical optimization architecture designed around decoupled operational planes, feedback-driven scheduling, and isolated state refinement. At Level 1, a Dual-Engine Controller monitors population Shannon entropy and empirical fitness…

items.title: Phase-Tunable Liouvillian Topology: Dual Winding Structures and Skin Effects
items.summary: Liouvillian skin effects are usually associated with dissipation whose rates favor unidirectional flow. In this work, we show that directional edge localization can emerge even when population exchange between sites is exactly balanced, with a single tunable phase parameter $α$ deciding their direction and a dual winding structure deciding their nature. Although this number-conserving bath is known for eigenstate selection, we demonstrate here that its phase controls a steady current, which Hamiltonian hopping…

items.title: Claw-free perfect graphs are chromatic-choosable
items.summary: We prove that every claw-free perfect graph $G$ satisfies $\ch(G)=χ(G)=ω(G)$. More strongly, if $S$ is a clique of simplicial vertices of $G$ and $k\geω(G)$, every proper precoloring of $S$ extends to a proper coloring of $G$ from arbitrary lists of size $k$ on $V(G)\setminus S$. items.title: Appointed-Time Fault-Tolerant Fast Terminal Sliding Control for UAVs with a Tracking Error-Based Disturbance Observer
items.summary: This paper addresses the critical challenge of high-performance fault-tolerant tracking control for quadrotor UAVs under complex conditions including external disturbances, parameter uncertainties, and actuator faults. A synergistic control framework is proposed by decoupling the system into position and attitude loops, each governed by the following three innovations. First, an Appointed-Time Prescribed Performance Function (AT-PPF) is developed to strictly constrain the tracking error within a predefined funnel…

items.title: Far-field Layers of Steady State for Viscous and Heat-conductive Gas
items.summary: We study the vanishing heat conductivity limit of radially symmetric stationary solutions to the non-isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the exterior of a ball under an inflow boundary condition. A distinctive feature of this singular limit is the formation of a far-field layer whose transition region moves toward spatial infinity as the heat conductivity tends to zero. We establish the existence and uniqueness of stationary solutions with the uniform estimates with respect to the heat…

items.title: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention
items.summary: Long-horizon reasoning and agentic workloads strain KV-cache capacity and decode attention throughput. We present Jet-QSparse, a training-free method that combines compact NVFP4 cache storage with native FP4 query-key computation on Blackwell tensor cores. A dense scan scores the full key history and selects 128-token blocks for sparse FP16 value aggregation with FP32 accumulation, preserving higher precision in the output-forming step while enabling contiguous tile loads. Calibrated key centering and at most two…

items.title: Leap-VLA: High-Rate Robot Control from a Low-Rate VLM Backbone
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models re-encode the full observation through a multi-billion-parameter vision-language model (VLM) at every control step, even though scene semantics evolve at roughly 1 Hz while reactive control requires 20-50 Hz. We present a VLA that decouples the two: a VLM runs as a low-frequency semantic anchor whose cached context is reused across control steps, while a flow-matching action expert operates at high frequency, consuming the cached semantics with a fresh, low-latency visual…

items.title: The Golden Quadruple: Four Reals Whose Differences Form a Geometric Progression, Rigidity of the Golden Ratio, and a Bohr Almost Periodic Cosine Sum
items.summary: Let $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. The set $\{0,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3\}$ is classical (Euclid, Elements XIII.8): by $\varphi^2=\varphi+1$ its six pairwise differences take the values $1,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3$, with multiplicities $1,2,2,1$. We write it as the golden quadruple $S=(F, F-a, F-b, F-a-b)$, $a=\varphi u$, $b=\varphi^2u$, $F>a+b$, and study its extremal and rigidity properties. No five distinct reals have all their positive differences in $\{u\varphi^n:n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$; this follows from a result…

items.title: PACT: Defending Recommendation against Promotional News Rewriting via Attack-Diverse Score Consistency
items.summary: Personalized news recommenders are increasingly vulnerable to LLM-powered promotional attacks, where content providers rephrase headlines to manipulate rankings without altering underlying facts. Defending against such manipulation requires covering a wide spectrum of LLM generators and optimization strategies--ranging from stylistic prompting to reinforcement feedback--without incurring prohibitive training or inference costs. In this work, we present PACT (Pooled Attack Consistency Training), a model-agnostic…

items.title: From Kination to Detection: Scotogenic Scalar Dark Matter
items.summary: We investigate scalar dark matter in the scotogenic model during an early kination-dominated epoch. The enhanced expansion rate causes earlier freeze-out and increases the relic abundance, opening viable dark matter masses from approximately $200~\mathrm{GeV}$ to $1~\mathrm{TeV}$ while reducing the need for co-annihilation with a nearly degenerate singlet fermion. Current indirect searches strongly constrain the $(100-200)~\mathrm{GeV}$ region, whereas much of the surviving parameter space can be probed by CTA…

items.title: Efficient Interpolation of the Bethe-Salpeter Hamiltonian at Arbitrary Momenta
items.summary: We develop an efficient reciprocal-space method to reconstruct the static Bethe-Salpeter (BSE) Hamiltonian at arbitrary crystal momenta from coarse first-principles grids. Bloch states are interpolated within an optimally smooth Wannier subspace, while the screened Coulomb interaction is reconstructed from the dielectric response. This decouples the electron-hole transition momenta and transferred momentum from the underlying ab initio sampling. We benchmark the method on monolayer hBN, monolayer MoS$_2$, and…

items.title: Latin cubes of order $4$ and $4320$-point quaternionic constructions in $\mathbb R^16$
items.summary: Possibly the most enduring lower-bound record for kissing numbers in dimensions greater than $8$ (excluding $24$) is $$ κ_{16}\geq 4320. $$ This lower bound is attained by a shell of the famous Barnes--Wall lattice, which was discovered in 1959. Besides this configuration, at least one alternative $4320$-point kissing arrangement is currently known. Recently, it was noticed that all these configurations can be described in terms of the so-called quaternionic construction, a general type of construction that was…

items.title: An exhaustion-aware product moment and zero-free half-planes for Hecke L-functions
items.summary: We refine the ordinary product moment in the cubic-theta comparison by allowing a returned prime product to be exhausted. The return stops either when the positive-prime length inequality holds or when the established prime-free ordinary estimate applies. Keeping the extracted central coefficients gives a local normalization inequality on a larger domain. On the critical ordinary-length interval this yields a net first-mean gain of $1/20000$. We prove the complementary-class, short-sum and algebraic comparison…

items.title: Beyond Source Compatibility: WebAssembly as a Stable ABI for ARINC 653 Applications
items.summary: Thirty years ago, ARINC 653 was introduced to provide a vendor-independent platform for software applications in Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA). A platform is characterized by a well-defined interface abstracting over implementation details; in the case of ARINC 653 this is an Application Programming Interface (API), defined on the source-code level. However, several aspects of this API - such as the memory layout and partially also the integer bit width of data types - remain implementation dependent, so…

items.title: Multi-quadrotor systems interconnected via structurally unknown forces and moments
items.summary: This work addresses the challenge of controlling multi-quadrotor systems subject to tight uncertain couplings. We consider interconnection forces and moments among the quadrotors to be state-dependent functions of the coordination errors, without assuming knowledge of their functional/parametric structures, e.g., no linear-in-parameters assumptions are made. We only rely on general state-dependent quadratic bounds valid for several Euler-Lagrange mechanical systems. We propose a coordination strategy embedding…

items.title: What Breaks and What Comes Back: Capability Damage and Recovery in Depth-Pruned Small Language Models
items.summary: Depth pruning removes whole Transformer blocks to make a language model smaller and faster, but the damage is not spread evenly across what the model can do, and a short fine-tuning run, called healing, decides what comes back. We measure this for small models used as agents. Four instruction-tuned models of 1.2-1.7B parameters (Llama-3.2-1B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, SmolLM2-1.7B and OLMo-2-1B) are pruned and healed, and six capabilities are tracked: structured output, function calling, instruction following, mathematical…

items.title: ShiftRAG: Bypassing the Textual Bottleneck via Decoupled Learning and Continuous Soft Tokens
items.summary: Despite advances in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), suppressing hallucinations during complex reasoning remains a persistent challenge. We identify that existing RAG pipelines suffer from a textual bottleneck: by passing only raw text to the generator, they discard discriminative signals of the retriever. Furthermore, recent attempts to unify retrieval and generation within a single LLM induce severe objective conflict and exacerbate the rank collapse of decoder-only architectures, degrading performance on…

items.title: From MHV Gravity Amplitudes and Hodges map to Pentad Varieties
items.summary: We study some geometric aspects behind the Hodges matrix appearing in the context of scattering amplitudes for the $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity. Through a vector bundle construction, we show that the Hodges matrix gives rise to a canonical rational map from the two-step flag variety to symmetric matrices, called the $\textit{Hodges map}$. This construction allows to define the amplitude geometrically: its vanishing locus is a divisor - the $\textit{MHV gravity divisor}$. Inspired by the Hodges map, we introduce…

items.title: Three-Dimensional FDTD Simulation of Superconducting Terahertz Emitters Using an Effective Medium Approximation
items.summary: Compact and tunable terahertz (THz) sources with controllable polarization are sought for high-speed links, spectroscopy, and imaging. In superconducting THz emitters based on a cuprate Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+δ}$, which have the potential to satisfy such properties, modeling often relies on heavy nonlinear solvers or empirical isotropic dielectrics, obscuring anisotropy, plasma response, and bias dependence. We derive an anisotropic, dispersive effective permittivity from the Lawrence-Doniach model for a…

items.title: On the nonvanishing of Floer lasagna modules
items.summary: In this paper, we establish several nonvanishing results for Floer lasagna modules $\mathcal{FL}(W,K)$ for a smooth compact connected oriented $4$-manifold $W$ and a knot $K\subset \partial W$, via the evaluation maps to link Floer homology. We first establish a general criterion: if a certain Heegaard Floer cobordism map associated with a smooth $4$-manifold $W$ is nonzero, then $\mathcal{FL}(W,U)\neq 0$, where $U\subset \partial W$ is a local unknot. items.title: Quantum Black Holes in Non-Linear Electrodynamics
items.summary: Techniques of AdS/CFT correspondence and braneworld holography have proven to be a useful tool for solving the problem of semi-classical gravity where quantum matter provides the back-reaction to classical spacetime geometry. In this paper, we apply this approach to Einstein gravity coupled to RegMax nonlinear electrodynamics and construct novel type of charged quantum black holes. We then discuss their thermodynamics and horizon structure.

items.title: Who Schedules Agent Memory? A Sidecar Approach to Long-Horizon Tasks
items.summary: As large language model agents increasingly undertake complex, long-horizon tasks, memory has become an important component for supporting sustained decision-making and action. Existing methods primarily focus on memory storage, updating, and retrieval, but often overlook how memory scheduling affects task execution: the main agent must identify memory needs, initiate retrieval, and wait for results while advancing the task, increasing both scheduling burden and execution time. To address this problem, we propose…

items.title: Model-Based Learning of Latent Euclidean Embedding from Relational Data
items.summary: Visualizing and interpreting the dependence structure in relational data often benefits from geometric representations via low-dimensional Euclidean embeddings. However, existing approaches are typically restricted to specific response types, rely on burdensome high-dimensional nonconvex optimization, or lack uniform theoretical guarantees for simultaneous coordinate recovery. To address these limitations, we introduce a unified, distance-based latent space framework for both unipartite and bipartite relational…

items.title: Free energy of 2-spin spherical vector spin glasses
items.summary: We compute the limit of free energy of 2-spin spherical vector spin glasses with possibly non-convex interaction and couplings satisfying a finite fourth-moment assumption. The couplings need not be Gaussian. The limit is given by a logarithmic-determinant variational formula, equivalently by a finite-dimensional matrix Dyson equation, and its zero-temperature limit yields the ground-state energy. The limiting formulas depend only on the covariance of the couplings. We also study fluctuations: at an interior…

items.title: On the complexity of isomorphism problems for tensors, groups, and polynomials V: over commutative rings
items.summary: Tensors over commutative rings naturally appear in number theory, geometry, and group theory. For example, $2\times 2\times 2$ tensors over $\mathbb{Z}$ form the starting point of Bhargava's celebrated works generalising Gauss's composition law (Bhargava, Ann. Math., 2004). Symmetric tensors over $\mathbb{Z}$ are central to the classification of Calabi--Yau threefolds (Yau, Commun. Pure Appl. Math., 1978; Wall, Invent. Math., 1966), geometric objects of significance in string theory. Additionally, tensors over…

items.title: Partition statistics and universal mixed mock modular forms
items.summary: In this note, we construct combinatorial statistics in terms of partitions, overpartitions, and two-color partitions and relate the corresponding generating functions to the universal mock theta functions. Our framework primarily builds on two $q$-series identities of Fine.

items.title: Representation-Aware Closed-Surface Parameterization: Exact Sensitivity Analysis and Pole-Aware Planar Preconditioning
items.summary: Surface parameterization is a fundamental task in geometry processing and shape analysis. For topologically closed surfaces, it is common to parameterize them onto a standardized closed domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a prime example being a unit sphere for genus-0 closed surfaces. Many mapping methods use planar projections and perform computations on the plane rather than directly on the 3D surface. However, perturbations introduced before projection or geometric evolution propagate through the computation and…

items.title: Free energy of spherical vector spin glasses
items.summary: We identify the limit free energy of spherical vector spin glasses by a variational formula. The covariance function need not be convex. Using the global symmetry of the spin configurations, we introduce a family of constraint measures that gives a disintegration of the original spin distribution. We first identify the limit free energy of each constrained model and then apply the Laplace method to recover that of the original model.

items.title: Vision-based Sensing of Urban Environment using Hardware-Software co-design at Scale
items.summary: Urban environmental monitoring is crucial for climate-adaptive cities, yet current approaches rely heavily on human inspection, overhead remote sensing, or limited terrestrial RGB imagery, thereby lacking comprehensive multispectral perspectives at street level. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces UrbanScapes, an adaptable and flexible hardware-software co-design platform for large-scale, vision-based sensing of urban environments. items.title: On Certain Congruences for Partition $k$-Tuples with $5$-Cores
items.summary: Let $A_{t,k}(n)$ denote the number of partition $k$-tuples of $n$ with $t$-cores. Using fifth-order modular equations and the Atkin $U_5$-operator, we prove the congruences $A_{5,125i+21}(25n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^3}$ for $r\in\{9,14,19,24\}$, $A_{5,125i+41}(25n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^3}$ for $r\in\{19,24\}$, and $A_{5,125i+111}(125n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^4}$ for $r\in\{39,64,89,114\}$, which were stated by Tang \cite{tang2025iterative}.

items.title: A note on the quantization of M2-branes on local Calabi-Yau manifolds
items.summary: In this note we present a detailed computation of the BPS states from M2-branes wrapping 2-cycles in local Calabi-Yau manifolds, at the level of brane quantization. For the cases of local Calabi-Yau threefolds, the supersymmetric quantum mechanics is the 1d $\mathcal{N}=4$ non-linear sigma model. We achieve systematic, physical interpretations of refined Gopakumar-Vafa (GV) invariants, first for the curve classes with fixed geometric genus, and then for curves whose geometric genus jumps. The BPS states of 5d…

items.title: Weighted $L^q$-$L^r$ estimates of a generalized Oseen evolution operator in exterior domains, with applications to the Navier-Stokes flow past a rigid body
items.summary: We consider a generalized Oseen evolution operator arising from time-dependent rigid motions in 3D exterior domains. Hishida and the present author established the regularity theory of the evolution operator by use of the $L^q$-$L^r$ smoothing estimates with a weight function $(1+|x|)^α$. The objective of this paper is to develop the weighted $L^q$-$L^r$ estimates globally in time. items.summary: Let $α$ be an element of $\Fq((1/T))$ which is not in $\Fq(T)$. We ask how small $\nrm{απ}$ can be made when $π$ runs over irreducible polynomials, and write $θ(α)$ for the largest exponent $θ$ such that $\nrm{απ}<|π|^{-θ}$ has infinitely many solutions. items.title: Constraints on Quintom Dark Energy Model with Matter Interaction
items.summary: The quintom model consisting of quintessence and phantom scalar fields with linear coupling to matter is explored and constrained by updated DESI and supernovae type Ia~(SNIa) observational data. The matter interaction is assumed only between phantom and matter and the quintessence self potential is in an exponential form. items.title: On the asymptotic distribution of the largest eigenvalue of unbalanced complex Jacobi ensembles
items.summary: Let $\mathbf{A} \sim \mathbb{C}\mathcal{W}_p(I,m)$ and $\mathbf{B} \sim \mathbb{C}\mathcal{W}_p(I,n)$ be two independent complex Wishart random matrices. In this work, we investigate the asymptotic distribution of the largest eigenvalue $θ_{\max}$ of the random matrix $\mathbf{J} = (\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{B})^{-1}\mathbf{B}$. items.title: From Weeks to Hours: Fast and Principled SFT Data Generation for Reasoning LLMs
items.summary: Reasoning-oriented post-training enables large language models (LLMs) to solve complex tasks via multi-step inference. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on high-quality reasoning traces is a particularly efficient approach, but its effectiveness depends critically on careful data curation. Existing pipelines rely on a costly generate-then-filter paradigm: large pools of long reasoning traces are produced by multiple teacher models and subsequently filtered for difficulty and diversity using additional LLMs, often…

items.title: Exact scalarization thresholds and onset laws for a nonminimally coupled scalar field on the Ellis wormhole
items.summary: We study a real scalar field nonminimally coupled to curvature on a fixed Ellis wormhole background. The scalar perturbation decouples at linear order, and the substitution $ x=a \tan z $ reduces its static radial equation to a trigonometric Pöschl-Teller problem. items.title: WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search
items.summary: We present WeSearch, a unified, model-centric retrieval framework for large-scale, continuously evolving content search. Prevailing methods assign documents fixed hierarchical Semantic IDs, implicitly assuming each document follows a single coherent semantic path-an assumption that often breaks down for multi-topic documents. WeSearch instead retrieves query-relevant clusters and then ranks atomic documents within the resulting query-specific candidate space, decoupling candidate pruning from fine-grained…

items.title: Estimating cosmogenic backgrounds in nEXO at SNOLAB using Geant4 and FLUKA
items.summary: The nEXO experiment was designed to search for neutrinoless double beta decay in the isotope $^{136}$Xe, using a five-tonne, isotopically-enriched liquid xenon time projection chamber (TPC). To meet nEXO's sensitivity goal, significant effort is placed on background mitigation strategies. Here, we evaluate the expected cosmogenic background rate for nEXO if placed at its preferred underground host site, SNOLAB. items.title: Order continuity of induced homomorphisms between free Banach lattices
items.summary: Let $T\colon F\to E$ be a bounded operator between Banach spaces and let $\overline T\colon FBL^{(p)}[F]\to FBL^{(p)}[E]$ be the lattice homomorphism induced by $T$ between the corresponding free $p$-convex Banach lattices generated by $F$ and $E$. items.title: Multivariate analogues of Ruijsenaars' hypergeometric function
items.summary: We construct multivariate analogues of Ruijsenaars' hypergeometric function as nested products of overlap coefficients between eigenfunctions of twisted primitive elements in representations of the modular double of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. The construction is a hyperbolic counterpart of the nested multivariate Askey--Wilson polynomials and functions. items.summary: Multi-messenger cosmology offers an independent path to stress-test the $Λ$CDM model as gravitational wave (GW) catalogs grow in size. items.summary: We study the local differential geometry of a Fourier-based modular-addition circuit in a one-layer transformer whose algorithm has previously been reverse-engineered. items.title: TAP-Out: Tracking Any Point in 360° via Outpainting
items.summary: Tracking points that leave the camera's field of view (FoV) requires reasoning about unobserved scene dynamics, a fundamentally different problem from tracking visible correspondences. We present TAP-Out, an offline method that makes this out-of-view (OOV) reasoning explicit by leveraging generative video outpainting as a world-model prior. items.title: Sealed, Lightweight gRPC-Based Muon Telescopes for Muography Applications
items.summary: Portable muon detection systems are increasingly in demand for muography applications in environments requiring flexible installation and transportability. We present the ongoing development and implementation of portable muon tracking systems based on glass Resistive Plate Chambers (gRPCs). The work addresses the fabrication and assembly of compact, position-sensitive RPC detectors, along with their performance when operated with a standard gas mixture and coupled to external front-end electronics and a scalable…

items.title: 5d SCFTs and Intersection Theory of Generalized Toric Threefolds
items.summary: Five-dimensional superconformal field theories are intrinsically strongly coupled fixed points that can be realized as M-theory on local Calabi-Yau threefolds with canonical singularities. The low-energy effective theory on their extended Coulomb branch is governed by a cubic prepotential, determined by the triple intersection numbers of divisors in the resolved geometry. For toric threefolds, dual to 5-brane webs, these numbers are computed combinatorially from the toric polygon. However, no such description has…

items.title: The recognition problem for 4-manifolds and the unknotting problem for 2-spheres in 4-manifolds
items.summary: We show that there is no algorithm to decide whether or not a given 4-manifold is PL homeomorphic to the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 . We also show that the TOP and PL unknotting problems for all surfaces in the connected sum of 7 copies of S 2 x S 2 are unsolvable.

items.title: Autoformalization for Ambiguous Inputs: Precision, Coverage, and Cost across SQL and Logical Forms
items.summary: Agentic systems translate natural-language requests into executable artifacts while managing ambiguity and inference cost. We evaluate seven autoformalization workflows on SQL and first-order logic benchmarks for ambiguous inputs. Across five SQL workflows, the raw model leads with F1 of 53.35% on AMBROSIA and 60.85% on AmbiQT. On AmP, DRIFT gains 15.98 F1 points over the raw model at 2.03 times its token cost, whereas LoC uses 18.65 times the raw model's tokens with lower F1. Within AutoCedar, structured…

items.title: Triple descent in quantum linear regression
items.summary: Quantum linear regression models, such as quantum extreme learning machines and quantum fidelity kernels, are trained on features that can only be estimated from finitely many measurement shots. Sampling noise is usually treated as a nuisance that more shots suppress; we show instead that it can fundamentally reshape the instabilities of the learning problem. As the number of measurement outcomes grows, the prediction error displays a triple-descent profile, with two peaks of fundamentally different origins. The…

items.title: SketchForge: Training-Free Scene-to-Vector Sketching via Decoupled Structure and Texture Optimization
items.summary: Converting a raster image into a resolution-independent, stroke-editable vector sketch while faithfully preserving both structural contours and tonal texture remains challenging: raster-space rendering pipelines are difficult to edit at the stroke level, while generation-from-scratch vectorization methods struggle to remain faithful to an arbitrary input image. We present SketchForge, a training-free framework that converts an input raster image into a resolution-independent SVG sketch through per-instance…

items.title: OmniPiano: Diverse Dexterous Piano-Playing Challenges for Standard, Robust, Safe, and Multi-Agent RL
items.summary: Dexterous robotic manipulation remains a major challenge in robotics, exemplified by piano playing, which requires coordinated control of fingers and provides a demanding testbed for reinforcement learning (RL). Although previous work established a benchmark for robotic piano playing, it is restricted to two hands and does not support unified evaluation. To address this gap, we introduce OmniPiano, a benchmark that provides one to up to five Shadow Hands and supports standard, robust, safe, and multi-agent RL…

items.title: Interacting scalar-fermion two-component dark matter in a gauged $\boldsymbolU(1)_B-L$ model
items.summary: We propose an interacting two-component dark matter model based on a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ extension of the Standard Model, which also accommodates neutrino masses through the type-I seesaw mechanism. The dark sector consists of a Dirac fermion $χ$ and a complex scalar $S$, which can both be stable without imposing an additional discrete symmetry and are directly coupled by a gauge-invariant Yukawa interaction. The resulting conversion, semi-conversion, and semi-annihilation processes lead to a genuinely coupled…

items.title: Shear Mapping in Python (SMPy): Modular, Extensible, and Accessible Dark Matter Mapping
items.summary: Understanding the Universe's large-scale distribution of dark matter is a central objective in the era of precision cosmology. A key technique for the study of dark matter is weak gravitational lensing: a phenomenon where light from distant galaxies is sheared as it passes through the gravitational field of a massive object, like a galaxy cluster. items.title: Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters
items.summary: We introduce the notion of cuspidal coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of local L-parameters. We give a complete classification and relate them to Lusztig's cuspidal local systems (or character sheaves). Under the categorical local Langlands conjecture, these sheaves are expected to correspond to supercuspidal representations supported at basic points. items.title: A local action for Kodaira--Spencer gravity
items.summary: A local action is given for Kodaira--Spencer gravity by solving a constraint on the complex structure deformation of a Calabi--Yau threefold in terms of a $(1,1)$ form as the new gravity field. The gauge algebra becomes a genuine $L_{\infty}$ algebra based on a Courant algebroid, while the gravity field and its linearized gauge transformations coincide with those of double field theory. On a real three-dimensional slice, the free action reduces to the Fierz--Pauli action for massless spin-2 plus the Kalb--Ramond…

items.title: An obstruction to generalised discrete torsion in string theory
items.summary: We reconsider the possibility of turning on generalised discrete torsion in orbifold compactifications, whereby different discrete torsion phases are attached to different fixed points of a given twisted sector. By an explicit inspection of the genus one and genus two vacuum amplitudes for the $T^6/\mathbb{Z}_2^2$ and $T^7/\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ cases, we show that this is not possible in String Theory. In fact, this generalised discrete torsion, although modular invariant at genus one, leads to an inconsistent…

items.title: Generalized Toric Threefolds from Scattering Diagrams and Broken Lines
items.summary: We present an explicit and practical description of Generalized Toric Calabi--Yau threefolds, which are associated with five-brane webs ending on seven-branes, using scattering diagrams and broken lines, based on ideas from arXiv:2410.04714 [hep-th]. Local theta-function algebras and their transition maps give explicit affine charts for opened (resolved) webs, extending familiar toric constructions to non-toric situations. We give a physical interpretation of the deformation parameters, in the case of one or…

items.title: Non-Invertible Charges for M-Theory
items.summary: The gauge charges of M-theory M2 and M5 branes almost resemble the charges of a 6-group. The charges of such a 6-group are expected to be modeled by operators with non-invertible fusion. We here consider non-invertible charge defects for continuous 2-groups and 6-groups, aiming to capture the gauge charges of M2 and M5 branes. We find a model for charges of a "pseudo 6-group" $\frak{G}$ which possesses remarkable similarities with known features of M2 and M5 branes, including: Hanany-Witten moves, the…

items.title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
items.summary: Decision models such as Jev have emerged as a highly promising paradigm for LLM agent systems, providing lightweight and reliable categorical reasoning for rapid System One execution. However, existing generation-oriented inference engines fail to support these workloads effectively, suffering from severe prefix recomputation overheads or distorted output probabilities. To address this challenge, we propose Flide, an efficient and exact inference engine that decouples the logical tree structure of a decision…

items.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.summary: Planning with world models enables test-time adaptation for embodied agents, offering superior generalization over direct policy learning. However, long-horizon tasks remain hindered by cumulative errors and search complexity. Existing hierarchical methods often use rigid macro-actions or latent skills, leading to brittle representations and limited fine-grained control. We introduce ID-WM (Implicit Dynamics World Models), a hierarchical world model that decouples state-space reachability from local control. Our…

items.title: On the Iwasawa invariants of admissible quadratic twists of elliptic curves at ordinary Eisenstein primes
items.summary: We study the Iwasawa $μ$- and $λ$-invariants of quadratic twists of rational elliptic curves at Eisenstein primes $p\geq 3$. We verify Greenberg's $μ=0$ conjecture for all such twists, which gives an Euler system free proof of Mazur's cotorsion conjecture, and study the $λ$-invariants when the twist is admissible in the sense of [GV00]. items.title: ReLift: Dense 3D Tracking as Lifted Trajectory Repair
items.summary: Dense 3D tracking from monocular video requires establishing point correspondences over time, estimating their depth, and inferring their trajectories during occlusion. Existing methods typically learn these tasks jointly, a demanding objective given the scarcity of 4D supervision. We show that strong pretrained 2D trackers and 3D geometry models provide an effective foundation: lifted trajectories, with occluded segments simply interpolated, already rival dedicated 3D trackers using the same geometry. However…

items.title: Anchor 1: Precise and Stable Humanoid Control for Whole-Body Manipulation
items.summary: Humanoid controllers have acquired increasingly diverse motor skills, yet translating these capabilities into precise and stable whole-body manipulation remains challenging. Manipulation tasks are sensitive to execution deviations -- even small errors or unintended steps can cause failure. Introducing Anchor 1, a whole-body controller for precise and stable whole-body manipulation, together with a benchmark spanning diverse coordination demands. items.title: Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation
items.summary: We prove that in rotationally invariant first-passage percolation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\geq2$, the passage time $T_n$ over a distance $n$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}[\exp(|T_n-μn|/n^{\frac{1}{2}(1-\varepsilon)})]\leq C$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, where $μ$ is the time constant. items.title: ACCT: Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer
items.summary: In real-world deployments, large language model (LLM) systems are increasingly evolving from single-model invocation toward heterogeneous deployments in which different models are dynamically invoked for inference. When the same context is reused across models, however, each newly selected target model typically has to process it again, repeatedly incurring substantial computational costs. items.title: Grassmannians of absolute Banach-Colmez Spaces
items.summary: We introduce Grassmannians of absolute Banach--Colmez spaces and prove the $k$-Grassmannian is perfectoid if and only if the space has slope $< 1/k$. For $d=1$, this proves a conjecture of Hansen--Mann. The key ingredient is a Plücker morphism, which realizes the $k$-Grassmannian of a slope $d/n$ space as a Zariski closed subspace of the projectivization of a slope $kd/n$ space. items.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data from Sliced Chebyshev Moments
items.summary: Research on practical differentially private (DP) synthetic data has largely focused on methods that approximately preserve low-dimensional marginals of a target distribution, and can thus only hope to preserve higher-dimensional, global structure as a lucky by-product. At the same time, existing methods that target global accuracy guarantees pay a price exponential in the data dimension, $d$. items.title: Constructing Lagrangian surfaces in all symplectic toric $4$-manifolds from multi-grid diagrams
items.summary: We present a new diagrammatic construction of Lagrangian surfaces in all symplectic toric $4$-manifolds from objects called multi-grid diagrams. These are a generalisation of triple grid diagrams for Lagrangian surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ wherein the underlying trisection is replaced by the more general notion of a toric decomposition. We give examples of multi-grid diagrams for Lagrangian surfaces in a range of symplectic toric $4$-manifolds, including Evans' recent non-squeezable Klein bottle in $S^2 \times S^2$.

items.title: Two-loop integrals for $t\bartγ$ production at hadron colliders in the leading-colour approximation
items.summary: We complete the calculation of the two-loop Feynman integrals required for the next-to-next-to-leading order QCD corrections to on-shell top--antitop production in association with a photon at hadron colliders, in the leading-colour approximation. items.title: Tests of equivalence principle violation in doubly coupled dark energy
items.summary: Recent work has shown that a simple form of coupled dark energy with a constant coupling produces a good fit to the DESI data. In this scenario, dark matter, but not baryons, couples to a scalar field, thereby violating the weak equivalence principle (EP). items.title: Proof-Carrying Evolution: Black-Box Search, White-Box Flight
items.summary: We study whether a language model can help design controllers whose behavior can be formally checked. items.summary: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. items.title: Nexus-VLA: Bridging Human and Robot Experiences via a Shared Hierarchical Semantic Latent Space
items.summary: Large-scale egocentric human videos provide rich and scalable manipulation experience for robot policy learning, yet substantial embodiment gaps in visual appearance, kinematic structure, and action spaces hinder effective knowledge transfer. items.title: Bootstrapping a Higher-Derivative Cosmological Collider: Borel-Laplace Resummation and Stokes Phenomena
items.summary: We develop a higher-derivative cosmological bootstrap for massive spectators with quartic dispersion, $ω^2\propto k^4$, revealing a new boundary-value problem for inflationary correlators. items.summary: We study series $L(x,s):=\sum_n ρ(n)e^{2πi n x}/n^s$, where $ρ(n)$ are Fourier coefficients of an automorphic form $φ$ for a discrete cofinite subgroup $Γ\subset \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$. items.summary: Anomalies of global symmetries can arise in long-range entangled quantum many-body systems and provide useful constraints on their dynamics. In this paper, we study anomalies of $d$-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) coupled to parameter spaces and their implications for ground-state degeneracies. items.title: Ramsey numbers $R(K_{1,4},K_{m,n})$ for small $m$
items.summary: We determine all currently unknown values of the generalized two-color Ramsey number $R(K_{1,4},K_{m,n})$ for $\min(m,n) \leq 8$. We also prove that the number $R(K_{1,4},K_{m,m})$ equals $26, 29, 31, 33$ for $m = 9, 10, 11, 12$ respectively.

items.title: Relaxation speed in quenched-random force fields
items.summary: Disorder is commonly expected to slow down relaxation, as in glasses and disordered magnets. items.summary: For $1\le i\le j\le k$, let $gr^3_2(K_i, K_j, K_k)$ be the least $n\in \mathbb{N}$ such that every rainbow triangle-free $3$-coloring of $K_n$ (using red, blue, and green) contains a red/blue $K_i$, a red/green $K_j$, or a blue/green $K_k$. items.title: Neutrino Oscillation in a Static Dihole Geometry
items.summary: We investigate neutrino flavor oscillations in the static equal-mass Majumdar-Papapetrou dihole geometry, restricting the propagation to the symmetry plane. items.summary: Turbulent cascades in high Reynolds number regimes span many decades in scale, which can be challenging for numerical simulations. Cascade models that use logarithmic discretization can help, but these have limited capabilities to describe spatial structures or real space details. items.summary: We prove that the quenched pressure of the Hopfield model with $K\simαN$ i.i.d. symmetric Rademacher patterns has a thermodynamic limit at every load $α\in(0,\infty)$, finite inverse temperature and uniform external field, with no replica-symmetry, order-parameter concentration or non-condensation hypothesis required. items.summary: We study the integer-valued membrane model on boxes $[-L,L]^d\cap\mathbb{Z}^d$ with zero boundary conditions. items.title: ReX-GG: a LLM Ensemble Pipeline for Relation-extraction and Graph Generation
items.summary: Current LLM ensemble frameworks focus on multi-step setups with additional modules for answer ranking, often opting for token and span analysis rather than structured outputs, leading to heavyweight architectures with potential fail states along the pipeline. items.summary: Conversational explainable AI (ConvXAI) agents often use GUS-style architectures with separate modules for intent recognition, dialogue management, and template-based response generation. items.title: Primordial black holes and gravitational waves from aligned axion inflation

items.title: From thermogravity to thermocosmology with a running non-conservation scale
items.summary: Thermogravity offers a novel approach to cosmic acceleration, deriving trace-free gravitational equations and matter non-conservation from thermodynamic processes in spacetime. items.title: On the generic case of Jiang's conjecture
items.summary: Jiang's conjecture predicts that if $π$ is a generic representation of a quasi-split $p$-adic group, then the $L$-parameter of the Aubert-Zelevinsky involution of $π$ must be trivial on $\mathrm{SL}_2$. items.title: On the modularity of residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2
items.summary: We use a new version of the Taylor--Wiles method, based on a tame analogue of the techniques introduced by Skinner--Wiles, to prove new modularity theorems for residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2 over totally real fields.

items.title: Latent-Lens: Visual Perception in Small Language Models Through Latent Communication
items.summary: Bridging independent vision-language models (VLMs) and small language models (SLMs) in a modular multi-agent system typically forces them to exchange information as discrete text, which creates a lossy bottleneck for spatial and fine-grained details. items.title: Reimagining Text-to-SQL: A Survey of Large Language Model Architectures and Strategies
items.summary: Text-to-SQL systems translate natural language questions into executable SQL queries, democratizing access to relational data. items.title: The Evolution of the Circumgalactic Medium after a starburst in DESI Post-Starburst Galaxies
items.summary: We present a statistical study of the cool circumgalactic medium (CGM) around massive post-starburst galaxies, traced by Mg II $λ\lambda2796,2803$ absorption in background quasar spectra from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2. items.summary: We prove joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function for shifts $ζ(s+id_jτ)$ with arbitrary nonzero real parameters $d_j$ whose absolute values are pairwise distinct, and show that these conditions are optimal. As a consequence, we establish generalized strong recurrence for every finite family of nonzero real parameters, meaning that the corresponding shifts of the Riemann zeta-function simultaneously approximate each other. items.summary: Altermagnetism (AM) is a novel collinear antiferromagnetic phase characterized by spin-polarized bands and zero net magnetization. However, realizing AM in monolayer hexagonal lattices is strongly constrained by lattice symmetry. Here, we propose a mirror-symmetry-based design principle and implementation scheme for realizing AM based on monolayer hexagonal lattices and validate it using holey graphyne (HGY) as a representative system. By examining hydrogenated nonmetal units X$-$H (X = B, C, N, P, and S)…

items.summary: We investigate the effect of an oscillating axion background on thermally induced vortex-antivortex production in the Abelian-Higgs model. Through its coupling to the gauge field, the axion sources an electromagnetic response in the presence of vortex magnetic flux, modifying the dynamics of the vortices. items.title: On sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of theta quotients
items.summary: Motivated by conjectures of Schlosser and Zhou on sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of infinite products, we study two families of theta quotients and their positive integral powers. We determine asymptotic formulas for their Fourier coefficients and use them to obtain explicit eventual periodic sign patterns. Our results provide new instances of the sign phenomena observed by Schlosser and Zhou and illustrate how dominant cusps determine the resulting sign patterns. items.title: DAPS: Dependency-Aware Premise Selection for LLM Theorem Proving
items.summary: LLM-based theorem proving in Lean 4 has advanced rapidly, but provers are difficult to leverage newly contributed lemmas, because retrieval skews toward popular foundational lemmas, leaving the right premises buried among hundreds of thousands of candidates. Existing neural selectors rank candidates by semantic similarity, with three intrinsic limitations: frequency-skewed retrieval, isolated pairwise ranking, and degradation on out-of-distribution queries such as competition problems and informal language. items.title: Composition factor algebras and finite representation type
items.summary: An Artin algebra is called a composition factor algebra if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. We prove that every composition factor algebra is representation-finite. This settles a conjecture of Auslander, Reiten and Smalø. We also give criteria for comma categories and factorization categories to be of finite representation type.

items.summary: Chemotactic aggregation can overcome diffusion and lead to finite-time blow-up in Patlak-Keller-Segel models. items.summary: We We explore the use of the Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS) algorithm as a numerical tool to study phase transitions and critical phenomena. By mapping physical systems such as Ising and spin-glass models directly onto Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs), and extending the analysis to both synthetic and trained architectures, we use a unified RBM framework to compare the performance of AIS against standard Monte Carlo methods in regimes characterized by strong fluctuations and complex energy landscapes. items.title: Probing dark sector with decihertz gravitational wave observations of compact binary inspirals in IndIGO-D
items.summary: We investigate the potential of decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) observations of compact-binary inspirals to probe atomic dark matter (aDM) and its interactions through an ultralight massive dark photon. We consider a scenario in which neutron stars accumulate DM charged under a dark Abelian massive vector mediator, leading to an additional long-range Yukawa interaction between compact objects and associated dipolar radiation. items.title: Irrationality of values of $L$-functions for real Dirichlet characters
items.summary: Let $χ$ be a non-trivial real Dirichlet character and $s$ be a sufficiently large integer. items.summary: Classic modeling of opinion dynamics via the Friedkin-Johnsen (FJ) model relies on the unrealistic assumption of synchronous communication among network users. Social media, however, exhibit extreme participation asymmetries: a vast majority of users silently observe, while a tiny minority creates and broadcasts most of the content. items.summary: Quantum algorithms for scientific computing are specified against access models such as block-encodings, sparse oracles, state preparations, and quantum random-access memories. Their concrete realization is deliberately left open, yet it is a research variable that changes both the numerical behavior and the resource cost of the program, so every reported conclusion is attributable to one realization. items.summary: We study deterministic and stochastic optimization over the Stiefel manifold, explicitly allowing iterates to deviate from the manifold rather than enforcing feasibility via retraction at each step. items.summary: We give an asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function in the $t$-aspect. This is a generalization of Selberg's asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of the Riemann zeta function. As an application, we observe the change and the stability of the weighted one-level density of zeros of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function.

items.summary: We prove strong uniqueness of tangent flows at the first singular time of a closed Ricci flow when one tangent flow is generated by a complete smooth asymptotically conical Ricci shrinker. items.summary: We establish improved local smoothing estimates for the Schrödinger equation on waveguides. items.summary: Latent dynamics learning has emerged as a prominent approach for Model Order Reduction (MOR) of time-dependent, parameterized Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). items.summary: We examine modular inversion of strict Grid certificates in a ceiling continued-fraction construction for the Erdős--Straus equation. items.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
items.summary: Pixel-space generative Transformers typically use one token per image patch, so capturing finer detail requires more tokens and makes global attention increasingly expensive. We observe that finer detail does not necessarily require more global communication: low-frequency structure benefits from global exchange, while high-frequency detail can be modeled locally. items.title: SwapBot: Tool-Centric Robot Manipulation via Interchangeable End-Effectors and Tactile Sensing
items.summary: Robot manipulation in everyday environments inherently involves substantial tool usage. Seemingly simple household tasks, such as cooking pan-fried tofu, require forceful cutting, delicate brushing, and precise placement using different tools under contact-rich interaction. Thus, the ability to autonomously swap and use task-appropriate tools is important for tool-centric manipulation. We introduce SwapBot, a modular, tool-centric end effector system featuring low-cost adapters that quickly convert common…

items.title: Toric codes all the way down: decoupling translation-invariant topological CSS codes in higher dimensions
items.summary: Topological Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes in more than two spatial dimensions offer features useful for fault-tolerant quantum computation, such as transversal non-Clifford gates and single-shot decoding, but a systematic understanding of them is still lacking. One approach is to decouple a code: map it to a stack of higher-form toric codes by a finite-depth local CSS-preserving Clifford circuit, possibly after adding ancillas. items.title: Every Token Needs Its Own Teacher: Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-distillation
items.summary: On-policy Self-distillation (OPSD) has proven effective for post-training large language models by constructing a teacher conditioned on privileged references. However, existing approaches keep the teacher fixed either throughout training by consistently exposing it to the full reference, or within each response by adaptively varying partial reference exposure only across responses. In this paper, we argue that neither of them is sufficient. Instead, every token needs its own teacher, as the teacher preference…

items.title: Presentations for sisters of one-cusped Picard modular groups
items.summary: We generalize a method devised by Mark and Paupert for finding group presentations of the single-cusped standard Picard modular groups $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_d)$, where $\mathcal{O}_d$ is the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(i\sqrt{d})$, to a more general class of lattices in $\text{PU}(2, 1)$. items.title: FARMS: A Verifiable Foundation for Automated Computational Science
items.summary: Automated computational science could accelerate discovery by selecting, adapting and developing numerical methods. This prospect requires mathematical knowledge that AI systems can interpret and reuse with explicit guarantees. Here we present FARMS, a faithful and efficient foundation that transforms computational mathematics into AI-ready computing knowledge. FARMS connects formal statements to source context, algorithmic meaning and quantitative guarantees through source preparation, reusable representations…

items.title: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
items.summary: As AI's mathematical capabilities rapidly improve, meaningful benchmarks are shifting from university-level problems and math olympiads to research-level mathematics. The Ramanujan Challenge is a benchmark comprised of research-level problems in number theory, including unpublished results and open conjectures. It presented concrete formulas for mathematical constants whose correctness can be checked numerically, while their proofs may require non-obvious mathematics. items.title: crush: Extensible Proof Automation for Lean
items.summary: Lean's rich expressiveness supports higher-order functions, inductive datatypes, and user-defined abstractions, making it challenging to translate proof obligations into first-order Satisfiability Modulo Theory (SMT) queries and reconstruct kernel checked proofs. We present crush, an extensible SMT-backed proof automation framework for Lean. To bridge the gap between Lean's higher-order constructs and the solver's first-order logic, crush uses defunctionalization to encode function values and their applications…

items.summary: An even lattice $L$ of signature $(2,1)$ is Petersson-rigid if the orthogonal group of its discriminant form acts absolutely irreducibly on the space of cusp forms of weight $\frac32$ for its Weil representation, a space of dimension at least two. items.title: Single-Temperature Ranked Greedy Cluster Exchange for Max-Cut on Two-Dimensional Tori
items.summary: Ground-state search in two-dimensional Ising spin glasses on large toroidal lattices remains challenging for local-update heuristics because rugged energy barriers impede relaxation across metastable states. Equivalent to zero-field toroidal Max-Cut problems, these spin-glass instances also serve as standard benchmarks for optimization heuristics. items.title: Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs
items.summary: AI has made remarkable progress in mathematics, solving challenging problems with machine-checkable proofs in Lean, yet typically relying on predefined mathematical definitions and formal specifications. This raises a natural question: can it reason rigorously about an unknown world? We introduce the Algebraic World Model (AWM), a framework that turns interaction with unfamiliar environments into explicit mathematical models supporting formal reasoning. items.title: Entropic Fluctuations in Quantum Statistical Mechanics: A Review
items.summary: The celebrated Evans--Searles, respectively Gallavotti--Cohen, fluctuation theorem concerns certain universal statistical features of the entropy production rate of a classical system in a transient, respectively steady, state. In this paper, we review and compare several possible extensions of these fluctuation theorems to quantum systems. items.title: A Simplified Born Rule for Cosmological Correlators
items.summary: Cosmological correlators are natural observables of the primordial universe and are related to wavefunction coefficients by the Born rule. For equal-time in-in correlators in flat spacetime, we prove that all double-boundary poles cancel for arbitrary graphs, including in theories with local derivative interactions. items.title: UNIONS: Red and blue alignments of DESI DR1 galaxies
items.summary: Intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxies are a dominant source of systematics in weak-lensing cosmological analyses, and direct measurements on spectroscopic samples are the primary source of priors on their amplitude. We measure the IA of galaxies from the first data release (DR1) of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) as a function of colour, stellar mass, and halo mass, by cross-correlating the DESI spectroscopic catalogues with the weak-lensing shape catalogue of the Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical…

items.title: TEMPEST - A modular Python-based thermophysical model for rough, irregularly-shaped airless bodies
items.summary: Comparing observed and predicted surface temperatures on airless planetary bodies is crucial for interpreting their surface processes, constraining activity, and deriving their surface properties. We present a new tool in this endeavour: TEMPEST (Thermophysical Evolution Model for Planetary Environment Surface Temperatures). It is a modular, open-source Python model for diurnal thermal evolution on irregular bodies. TEMPEST can reproduce non-Lambertian multiple scattering using arbitrary Bidirectional Reflectance…

items.title: Exponential Convergence of the Lifted Gradient Flow of the Bass Functional
items.summary: We establish multidimensional exponential convergence of the lifted Bass gradient flow in martingale optimal transport. Let $μ\le_{cx}ν$ be an irreducible pair, with compact convex target support, source support strictly inside the target support, and target density bounded above and bounded away from zero almost everywhere on its interior. items.title: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks
items.summary: Mathematical supervision for language models is typically flattened into isolated problem-solution pairs, discarding the curricular organization and evidential structure of the original sources. We introduce TOME-Math (Textbook-Oriented Mathematical Evidence), a large-scale corpus that converts 2,118 textbooks spanning the core areas of university-level mathematics subjects into approximately 380K structured proof-supervision records while preserving chapter order, proposition-proof links, dependency references…

items.title: Neural Network Approximation and Structural Complexity of Semilinear PDEs with Lower Bounds
items.summary: Neural networks are commonly used to learn the solution operators of PDEs such as the Navier-Stokes equations and viscous conservation laws. On standard benchmarks, moderately sized and often shallow networks achieve small errors that decay at algebraic rates with the network size. items.title: Limiting ESD for a weighted sample covariance matrix
items.summary: We study the empirical spectral distribution (ESD) of the random matrix $M_N=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N f(|πY_i|^2)\,Y_iY_i^\top$, where $π$ is a rank $k$ orthogonal projector on $\R^p$, $Y_1,\dots,Y_N$ are i.i.d. standard Gaussian vectors, and $k\to \infty$, $p/N\to γ$. items.title: Two-peak gravitational wave spectra from supercooled two-field phase transitions
items.summary: We study the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum generated by supercooled first-order phase transitions in two-field conformal models. We construct three representative toy models that capture the essential features of these models, derive analytical criteria for the existence of two-step transitions, and show how the two-field dynamics generate a genuine two-peak GW spectrum. items.title: Cosmological tests of chameleon dark energy with dark sector coupling
items.summary: Recent DESI measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations favor a value of $Ω_{\mathrm m}$ different from that preferred by Planck cosmic microwave background observations. Combined with supernova data, these observations suggest an evolving dark energy equation of state that crosses $w=-1$. Depending on the background of developers and users, conflicts between different goals may arise. items.title: A p-adic Valuation Calculus for Permutations with Restricted Cycle Lengths
items.summary: Let a_A(n) be the number of permutations of {1,...,n} all of whose cycle lengths lie in a set A. We develop a valuation calculus for these numbers. items.summary: Recent advances in video world models have enabled increasingly realistic and interactive virtual environments, opening new possibilities for player-customizable gameplay. items.summary: We study cohomological Donaldson-Thomas invariants of perfect complexes in a semistable degeneration of projective Calabi-Yau threefolds, with smooth components $X_1,X_2$ meeting along a smooth anticanonical surface $S$. items.title: Radiology Guideline-derived Decision Graph for Efficient Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: Radiological risk stratification and management planning are essential downstream tasks in medical imaging. Automating these tasks is challenging because clinical guideline criteria are distributed across prose, tables, and cross-referenced definitions. items.summary: We present Vampire-Hammer, a hammer for the Lean interactive theorem prover that discharges goals using the Vampire automated theorem prover and reconstructs proofs checked by the Lean kernel. Vampire-Hammer uses the Lean-auto framework to process goals and premises before dispatching them to Vampire for proof search. items.summary: Musculoskeletal robots combine compliant actuators with articulated skeletons, but exploring alternative configurations often requires repeated fabrication. items.summary: Gravitational waves as one approaches Schwarzschild null infinity are the core of our investigation, treated as the spin-weighted generalisation of a massless scalar field. items.summary: The two-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes equations with a shear-thickening viscosity driven by multiplicative noise are studied. items.summary: Accurate multi-organ segmentation in computed tomography (CT) is essential for computer-aided diagnosis, treatment planning, and disease monitoring. items.summary: Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) methods approximate sequences of probability distributions using populations of weighted samples and are widely applicable, including in Bayesian inference and particle filtering. items.title: Einstein's equations may explain the universe without dark energy
items.summary: Mathematicians have uncovered what they argue is a fundamental flaw in the standard model of the universe, potentially challenging the need for dark energy. Their calculations suggest that the mathematical framework used to describe cosmic expansion is inherently unstable and that the universe could accelerate naturally under Einstein's original theory of gravity. items.title: VERITAS Limits on Dark Matter Annihilation in the Galactic Center Halo

Existing memory mechanisms either retrieve history as implicit context, which remains constrained by context capacity and entangles static and dynamic information or consolidate history into explicit global representations, which struggle to model evolving dynamics and accumulate geometric errors. We show that there is a fully faithful functor from Berthelot's derived category of bounded complexes of D-dagger-modules with coherent cohomology into our new category.

items.title: The Umami Chaplygin Gas as a Unified Dark Fluid: Observational Constraints, Perturbative and Thermodynamic Stability Analysis
items.summary: We study a cosmological scenario in which the Universe contains standard baryonic matter, radiation, and a single unified dark fluid, the umami Chaplygin gas, which accounts for both dark matter and dark energy with no separate dark-matter component. items.summary: Spin ensembles show increasing promise for highly efficient quantum sensing and quantum technologies. However, protecting their coherent properties remains a significant challenge. Dynamical decoupling (DD) typically employs a sequence of fast pulses that aim to reduce the effect of unwanted system-environment interactions. items.summary: Background: Contemporary healthcare institutions generate daily very large amounts of data, which contain highly useful information for the improvement of work organization, planning and overall efficiency. items.summary: Byrne, Gluesing-Luerssen, and Ravagnani determined the number of codewords with a prescribed nonzero support in a linear maximum sum-rank distance code whose blocks have a common number of columns. items.summary: For an integer $h\geq2$, an edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $H^<$ is an $h$-uniform hypergraph with a linear ordering of its hyperedges. items.summary: We study the theoretical origin of scalar non-standard interactions (SNSI) in an \(A_4\)-symmetric Type-II seesaw model. The model contains an \(SU(2)_L\) scalar triplet \(Δ\) and a real scalar singlet \(S\). items.summary: Current Vision-Language Models (VLMs) frequently fail to recognize culture-specific concepts, especially from underrepresented regions. items.summary: Statistical downscaling is the task of reconstructing high-resolution meteorological fields from coarse inputs. items.summary: Multi-turn conversations with multimodal large language models (MLLMs) reuse input context, but long multimodal inputs increase time to first token (TTFT). items.title: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps
items.summary: While frontier vision-language models demonstrate strong capabilities in user interface (UI) navigation, their high inference costs prohibit everyday use. items.title: PDScope: Breaking the Prefill-Decode Seesaw for Memory-Bound MoE Inference
items.summary: Local deployment of MoE-based LLMs on CPU-GPU nodes is attractive for cost and privacy reasons, yet limited GPU memory forces most experts into CPU memory. items.title: The small Deborah number limit for the fluid-particle flows: incompressible case
items.summary: This work is devoted to the study of the hydrodynamic limit for the fluid-particle flows governed by the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck (VFP) equation coupled with the incompressible Navier-Stokes (INS) equation as the Deborah number approaches to zero. items.title: On the median of the beta distribution in relation to the median of the gamma distribution
items.summary: The median of the beta distribution has no closed form, but it is closely tied to the median of the gamma distribution. Kerman's approximation has the ratio form $g(α)/(g(α)+g(β))$ with $g(x) = x - 1/3$, a lower bound on the gamma median, and it is a lower bound on the beta median for $1/3 < α< β$. items.title: Joint Rigid Alignment and Morphable Reconstruction from Partial 3D Face Scans
items.summary: Aligning a partial, real-world 3D face scan to a canonical representation requires solving two coupled problems at once: estimating the rigid pose that brings the scan into a common frame, and completing the facial shape in regions the scan never observed. Existing pipelines typically decouple these steps, running a generic point-cloud registration front end followed by a separate non-rigid fitting or deformation stage. items.title: The inverse local-relative correspondence and the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation
items.summary: We prove the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation for the local Gromov--Witten theory of smooth weak del Pezzo surfaces, by identifying its unique formal solution with the inverse of the local-relative correspondence. We construct this inverse through an associative set-partition convolution and establish the identification using Zagier's recursion for the Bloch--Okounkov $n$-point function. The proof applies in all genera and includes non-toric surfaces.

items.title: CA2 numbers and the Riemann hypothesis: a numerical investigation of Ramanujan's inequalities
items.summary: Robin's criterion reduces the Riemann hypothesis to an inequality for colossally abundant (CA) numbers, and Wu's theorem reduces the test further to the subclass CA2. We study this reduction numerically and consider smaller subsets on which the same criterion remains sufficient. items.title: Sensing Fast and Distant Targets in Fractional Overspread Channels with Zak-OTFS and Modular Arithmetic
items.summary: Delay-Doppler (DD) modulations, such as Zak-transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation, represent the channel as a sparse set of delay and Doppler shifts, which makes them well suited for radar sensing. Sensing with a single DD frame, however, is unambiguous only when the channel spread factor, i.e., the product of the delay and Doppler spreads, is less then one. items.title: Complete quasinormal modes of Type-D black holes. II. Extremal Kerr black holes
items.summary: We develop a double-confluent Heun method that extends our previous study of complete quasinormal-mode (QNM) spectra of Type-D black holes to extremal Kerr black holes. Radial boundary conditions and angular regularity determine the gravitational frequencies at extremality. Compared with earlier spectra restricted to the conventional Riemann sheet, analytic continuation across frequency branch cuts reveals additional QNMs on unconventional Riemann sheets. items.title: The Korean Space Telescope (KST): A Dedicated Space Observatory for the Dark Universe
items.summary: The Korean Space Telescope (KST) is a next-generation 1.4-meter wide-field space observatory, a dedicated probe of the dark sector. items.summary: We investigate the diphoton excesses near $152~\mathrm{GeV}$ accompanied by missing transverse momentum (MET) in the Type-I two-Higgs-doublet model extended by a complex scalar singlet, whose imaginary component serves as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone dark matter (DM) candidate $χ$. items.summary: We study planar four-point scattering amplitudes on the Coulomb branch of $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory, focusing on multi-parameter families of massive kinematics.
