items.title: Modular Bayesian Foundation Models: Bayesian time series encoders for OOD detection, routing and forecasting
items.summary: Industrial systems continuously generate time series that vary in sampling frequency, scale, dynamics, and operating regime. Consequently a single time-series foundation model may not be able to represent all regimes effectively and retraining a large model for every new dataset or regime shift is computationally expensive. Modular foundation models address this issue by reusing specialised encoders trained on diverse datasets and by allowing the expansion of capabilities through the addition of new experts. This…

items.title: Large deviations for random walks generated by countable groups: a unified approach
items.summary: We present a unified treatment of various large deviation principles in the context of random walks induced by actions of countable groups. The fundamental notion undergirding the global perspective is that of weakly almost additive random walks, inspired by earlier works on the metric geometry of group actions as well as by recent developments in the theory of nonadditive thermodynamic formalism. items.title: Rethinking GFlowNet Training: Negative Reinforce Dynamics
items.summary: Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets) are models that learn to sample discrete objects proportional to a target reward. They are trained by minimizing balance errors over sampled trajectories, which inherently ties correctness to exploration: if a region is not visited, balance cannot be enforced there. items.title: Non-concordant 2-links in simply-connected 4-manifolds
items.summary: We construct an infinite family of smooth 2-component links of 2-spheres $Σ_k\subset S^2\times S^2$ whose respective components are smoothly concordant but which are pairwise not topologically concordant in any topological $\mathbb{Z}$-homology cobordism. In particular, the $Σ_k$ are pairwise non-concordant in $(S^2\times S^2)\times[0,1]$.

items.title: Coexistence of superconductivity and magnetic order in BaFe$_2$S$_3$: evidence for orbital-selective delocalization
items.summary: Understanding how superconductivity emerges from correlated electronic states is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. items.summary: Gravitational-wave observations of compact binaries offer a direct way to test whether gravity admits polarizations beyond the two tensor modes of general relativity. items.summary: Let $G$ be a quasi-split reductive group over a finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. items.summary: We extend the notion of non-local almost minimal sets introduced in [Dipierro, Valdinoci, and Villa, J. Math. Pures Appl. items.summary: We study the arrival time equation of the mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group. items.summary: Particle Gibbs samplers with backward sampling are widely used for sampling the smoothing distribution of state-space models, but, with few particles, the new trajectory often coincides with the current one at many time steps. items.summary: We prove that every smooth well formed Fano or Calabi-Yau weighted complete intersection admits a nef-partition. As an application, we establish the existence of weak Landau-Ginzburg models for all such Fano weighted complete intersections.

items.summary: Language models are increasingly being deployed in regulated settings, where a model must apply given rules to the facts of a situation to determine a verdict. items.summary: Inspired by work in Seiberg--Witten and Heegaard Floer homology, Dunfield, Schütz, and the author constructed an abelian "local equivalence group" built from pairs of chain complexes, and a homomorphism from the smooth concordance group to this group that uses the odd Khovanov complex and the Bar-Natan deformation of the even Khovanov complex. items.title: Timestral
items.summary: We introduce Timestral, a family of four time series foundation models for probabilistic forecasting, with 5M, 28M, 123M, and 209M parameters. Timestral sets a new state of the art on GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, where Timestral-209M and Timestral-123M take the top two places on every metric. items.title: Systolic pants decompositions with polynomial growth
items.summary: We investigate improved bounds on the kissing number of a hyperbolic surface under the assumption that the systole set contains pants decompositions with volume growth constraints. Namely, when the dual graph of the pants decomposition has polynomial volume growth, we obtain a power-savings improvement for the upper bound on the kissing number in terms of systolic length. items.title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging. We introduce OpenFrontiers, a cross-disciplinary resource that combines a structured corpus of open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of recently resolved problems in mathematics. items.title: Extending the W3C Data Privacy Vocabulary to Cover the German Health Data Use Act - Lessons Learned
items.summary: Finding, sharing, and reusing data requires common interoperable vocabularies to adequately describe machine-actionable data policies. Semantic Web standards are a proven way to express such information describing data access and reuse. Narrative descriptions get a stable and agreed meaning by formal definitions of terms that have a globally unique identifier. items.title: GTFormer: A Syntax-Free Graph Network Alternative to Transformers for 8192$\times$ Length Extrapolation in Linear Time
items.summary: Self-attention mechanisms have established the Transformer as the dominant backbone across natural language processing, source code intelligence, and automated theorem proving. However, all-to-all pairwise token comparison enforces a quadratic $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ compute and memory barrier alongside severe softmax attention dilution as sequence length $N$ scales beyond the training horizon. items.title: Orthogonal and Parametrized Multi-Attribute Steering of LLMs
items.summary: Activation steering offers an effective and efficient way to modify an LLM's behavior at inference time. However, it remains unclear how to apply steering such that the signal is consistently strong and the steering strength has a universally interpretable meaning. We address this first by identifying the most steerable interval for each steering vector and rescaling the steering range accordingly. items.title: Coordinated and Uncoordinated Channel Tracking for High-Rate IoT in Distributed Massive MIMO With Low-Resolution ADCs
items.summary: This paper investigates dynamic channel tracking for high-rate Internet of things (IoT) in distributed massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) with low-resolution analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), where pilot and data activities are decoupled, pilots are reused, and mobile channels evolve across access slots. items.title: New Developments in Diagrammatic Monte Carlo for Interacting Lattice Fermions: Efficient Algorithms and Applications
items.summary: This thesis develops diagrammatic methods for thermodynamic and subsystem quantities of interacting lattice fermions, providing reference calculations for quantum simulators and many-body approximations. I formulate an inverse-flavour expansion about a self-consistent Hartree saddle, enumerate non-Gaussian diagrams, and use a discrete Lehmann representation to integrate selected internal vertices analytically. items.title: DREAM: Delay-Resistant Acceleration with Momentum
items.summary: With exact, delay-free gradients, Nesterov's accelerated gradient (NAG) achieves optimal $\sqrtκ$ dependence for $L$-smooth, $μ$-strongly convex objectives, where $κ=L/μ$; heavy-ball (HB) achieves the same scaling on strongly convex quadratics. In asynchronous and distributed settings, gradients can be inexact, with delays varying across workers and iterations. items.title: ETAMem: Decoupling and Aligning Heterogeneous Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents
items.summary: Long-term memory enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to maintain coherent and personalized interactions across extended conversations. However, existing memory systems face two key challenges: (1) Information Entanglement, where heterogeneous information is mixed within coarse-grained memory units; and (2) Organizational Mismatch, where memory structures based primarily on semantic similarity may overlook other associations. items.title: Chaos picture of spin glasses
items.summary: The chaos picture is a novel, coherent, and intuitive theoretical framework for spin glasses, reconciling the 40-year-old droplet vs. replica symmetry breaking debate. First, we argue the formation of a hierarchical energy landscape by pinning and dynamic filtering of random droplets. As the temperature decreases, the chaos picture describes a progressive freezing of scale-dependent droplets in real space, which mirrors a hierarchical free energy landscape fracturing process in phase space. items.title: Spectral $L^2$-bounds on Eisenstein series and Diophantine properties of quadratic forms
items.summary: We give $L^2$-bounds with respect to the height of the spectral parameter for Epstein zeta functions $\mathrm{Z}_Q(s)$ and non-holomorphic Eisenstein series $E_{\mathfrak{c}}(s,z)$ attached to the Hecke congruence subgroup $Γ_0 (p)$ of prime level $p$. items.title: Typical Kakeya-type sets and their typical code sets
items.summary: We study properties of compact Besicovitch sets and other Kakeya-type sets which are typical in the sense that the exceptions form a meager set in the Baire category sense in a suitable metric space. The main motivation comes from the known fact that typical compact Besicovitch sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ have minimal Hausdorff dimension among all Besicovitch sets of $\mathbb{R}^n$. items.title: Can Complementary Signals Bridge Similarity Islands? Manifold-Augmented Graph Embedding for Multimodal Recommendation
items.summary: Multimodal Recommender Systems (MMRS) leverage rich item features to mitigate data sparsity, yet similarity-driven graph construction and propagation can favor semantically similar substitutes over functionally related complements. When behavioral associations connect semantically distant items, complementary signals can remain geometrically isolated, yielding fragmented "Similarity Islands" and semantic drift when standard propagation is applied. items.title: A zero-density estimate for the symmetric square $L$-functions in the weight aspect
items.summary: In this paper, we prove a zero-density estimate for the symmetric square $L$-functions associated with Hecke eigencuspforms in the weight aspect. The proofs are based on the mollified second moment of these $L$-functions.

items.title: Algebraic Completeness of Feynman Premeasures: The Henstock-Kurzweil Path Integral and Operator Wick Calculus in Lean 4
items.summary: We formalize in Lean 4 the gauge closure of the Feynman functional integral for the free field without Wick rotation. First, the restriction to box divisions is removed via a direction bound and a uniform Riemann-sum estimate for all $δ$-fine cylindrical divisions. Second, the coordinate measure on $\mathbb{R}^k$ is identified with the standard Gaussian one. Third, the Saks-Henstock lemma and additivity are proved. items.title: Tuning La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 magnetic anisotropy via interfacial coupling in homometallic trilayers
items.summary: In this work we explore the complex magnetic behaviour of SrMnO3/La0.7Sr0.3MnO3/SrMnO3 trilayers combining magneto-optic Kerr effect (MOKE) and magneto-resistance measurements. The interplay of structural and orbital reconstruction and the competition of ferromagnetism/antiferromagnetism at the interfaces is responsible of a variety of complex magnetic properties, highlighting the use of heterostructures as an effective strategy to tune and control magnetic behaviour. items.title: Free-vortex-wake dynamics of airborne wind energy kites in crosswind flight
items.summary: The wake of an airborne wind energy kite is shaped by its crosswind path and, for on-board generation, by the slipstreams of its rotors, and in farms it reaches downstream units. It is computed here by a vortex step method with a time-marching free vortex wake, implemented by the authors in their open-source code OpenFAWE with a lumped-mass tether, actuator-disc rotors releasing vortex rings and several kites. items.title: Perfect sampling of Ising spin glasses with bounding chains
items.summary: We study perfect sampling algorithms for Ising spin glasses based on coupling from the past and bounding chains, on several graph families and coupling distributions. For the single-site bounding chain, we establish coalescence in $O(n\log n)$ updates under Dobrushin conditions. On sparse random graphs, our numerical results suggest that efficient sampling extends throughout the tree-uniqueness regime, with a slowdown beyond this threshold. items.title: TRUCO: A Scalable Lock-Free Algorithm for Parallel Contour Extraction
items.summary: Extracting binary contours and their containment hierarchy is a fundamental step in many computer vision pipelines. While the standard Suzuki--Abe algorithm is inherently sequential, existing parallel tracers neither preserve its exact contours nor compute their hierarchy. This paper presents TRUCO (Threaded Raster Unrestricted Contour Ownership), a lock-free parallel algorithm for multi-core CPUs that produces the exact output of Suzuki--Abe. items.title: Effective Gromov-Witten computations for GKM spaces and a semisimple application
items.summary: We report a major update to our original software GKMtools and record multiple improvements in the computation of Gromov--Witten invariants of GKM spaces. This includes a refined divisor equation that reduces the complexity from exponential to linear in the number of marked points, three tricks to accelerate the computation of curve class relations in the GKM graph, and an implementation of Mihalcea's algorithm for homogeneous varieties using the equivariant quantum Chevalley formula. items.title: Watermark Basins: Black-Box Detection of Distilled LLMs
items.summary: Proprietary language models and their reasoning traces are vulnerable to API-based distillation, where an adversary trains a student model on the teacher model's outputs. To obtain evidence of distillation, model providers can watermark the teacher's outputs, aiming to leave a radioactive signal in the student's outputs. items.title: Explicit Serre weights for modular Galois representations of $U(2)$
items.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $G$ be a rank two definite unitary group as defined by Barnet-Lamb et al. in [2]. In this article, we determine explicit modular local Serre weights for mod $p$ Galois representations $\barρ_h$ associated to eigenforms $h$ of $G$, with arbitrary weights and small slopes. items.title: Sharp helical maximal estimates in all dimensions
items.summary: We establish sharp $L^p$ maximal estimates for averages over smooth nondegenerate curves in $\mathbb R^n$ for $p>n$. More precisely, we show that for any nondegenerate curve $γ$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and the associated maximal operator \begin{equation} M f(x):=\sup_{t>0} \Big|\int_{-1}^1f(x-tγ(s))χ(s)\,\mathrm{d}s\Big|, \end{equation} the estimate \begin{equation} \| Mf\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}\lesssim_{γ,p,n} \|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)} \end{equation} holds for all $p>n$. items.title: Vision-Language-Action or World-Action? Just Action Models
items.summary: The vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action model (WAM) communities debate whether control policies should inherit pretrained knowledge from vision-language models or from visual generators. items.title: QNETSIM for memory assisted design of satellite and hybrid quantum networks
items.summary: Space-based quantum information networks require simulation tools that capture orbital dynamics, probabilistic quantum operations, and classical coordination. We introduce QNETSIM, a modular discrete-event simulator for the design and performance evaluation of satellite and hybrid space-ground quantum networks. items.title: Searches for new particle physics by methods of classical and neutrino astronomy
items.summary: Selected astrophysical methods for testing particle-physics models are reviewed. items.title: Irreducibility Testing of Sparse Polynomials over Integers is NP-hard and Probabilistic Polynomial Time
items.summary: In this paper, we prove that irreducibility testing for sparse polynomials in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ is coNP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions. items.title: SFE-O: An Ontology for Knowledge-Grounded AI in Supercritical CO$_2$ Biomass Extraction and Fractionation
items.summary: Supercritical CO$_2$ extraction (CO$_2$-SFE) offers a sustainable route for recovering high-value compounds from biomass while limiting the use of conventional organic solvents, but its design and interpretation require heterogeneous knowledge spanning biomass properties, operating conditions, mass transfer, and product fractionation, typically fragmented across technical reports, engineering models, external databases, and expert practice. items.title: Decoupling Procedural and Outcome Fairness in Seed Allocation for Influence Maximization
items.summary: On online social platforms, equal seed access to interventions can yield unequal group outcomes through social spillovers, so an access audit alone can miss outcome disparities. items.summary: We study statistics of transport properties in a system of two quantum chaotic cavities coupled in series through a tunable junction and connected to reservoirs with asymmetric leads. items.title: Tessera: Structure-Completed Evidence Units for Web Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: Web retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) splits a page into fixed-size text chunks or, in recent visual pipelines, screenshot tiles, and the retrieved item serves at once as the unit of indexing, ranking, and reading. items.summary: We prove that every strict Calabi--Yau threefold of Artin--Mazur height one over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0 admits a projective lift to W(k). items.summary: We introduce a simple functional of algebra-valued fields with definite Lorentz properties that is kernel-free yet it encodes the structure of tree-level scattering amplitudes. items.title: Guided-RLVR: Guided Exploration in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has shown strong empirical gains in improving the reasoning ability of large language models (LLMs) on tasks such as mathematics and programming. However, recent studies have shown that RLVR rollouts often collapse onto a narrow set of reasoning trajectories, limiting the explored reasoning space. items.title: Linear-Time FPT Rectilinear Planarity Testing of Series-Parallel Graphs
items.summary: A planar graph is rectilinear planar if it admits a planar orthogonal drawing without bends. items.summary: The amplituhedron was introduced by Arkani-Hamed and Trnka (2014) to geometrically encode scattering amplitudes in high-energy physics. items.summary: The aim of this article is to study klt projective varieties such that the anticanonical bundle is semipositive from the differential-geometric point of view. items.title: The Disordered Universe 2025: Statistical Systems Out of Equilibrium
items.summary: These lecture notes provide an introduction to quantum spin glasses, with a particular emphasis on their application to open problems in cosmology and holography. items.title: Matter-Only Late-Time Acceleration via Barrow Entropy in Kaniadakis Statistics
items.summary: The Barrow correction to the horizon entropy changes the total number of microstates associated with the horizon, whereas the Kaniadakis correction provides an alternate statistical description of these microstates different from Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics. items.title: CaLLM: Continual Adaptation of LLMs via Non-Parametric Adapter Routing
items.summary: Continual adaptation of large language models (LLMs) to evolving task distributions while mitigating catastrophic forgetting remains an open problem. items.summary: How many fixed points does belief propagation have on a binary pairwise model? items.title: When Diffusion Recommenders Stop Sampling: Preserving Generative Diversity
items.summary: A user history can admit multiple plausible next interactions, yet conventional sequential recommenders produce a single deterministic ranking. items.title: Smithsonian scientists just recreated the first 2 billion years of the Universe
items.summary: Scientists have created one of the largest and most detailed simulations of the early universe ever made, offering an extraordinary new glimpse into the cosmos shortly after the Big Bang. items.title: Developing a Speech Language Model for Basque
items.summary: Although the recent development of LLMs has paved the way for multi-modal interaction, minority languages face difficulties keeping pace. items.title: LingGS: Decoupling Feed-Forward Geometry Prediction from Camera Tracking for High-Fidelity Gaussian SLAM
items.summary: Achieving high-quality reconstruction and responsive camera tracking remains challenging for monocular RGB Gaussian splatting SLAM under a limited optimization budget. items.summary: Sparse general matrix-matrix multiplication (SpGEMM) is a key kernel in graph analytics, relational queries, and machine learning. items.title: A fully articulated humanoid dexterous hand with human-level joint structure enabled by linkage-based actuation
items.summary: Humanoid dexterous hands are a core component of embodied intelligence, enabling robots to translate high-level intent into rich and adaptive physical interaction. items.title: CVBL-CCTV-Face Dataset for Real-World Face Enhancement and Recognition in Surveillance
items.summary: In real-world surveillance settings, facial captures from closed-circuit television systems suffer from degradations such as low resolution, motion blur, noise, and occlusions, which undermine dependable face recognition. items.summary: Open Data Analysis Tool for Science and Engineering (ODAT-SE) is an open-source Python framework for inverse problems that are solved by repeated forward simulations. In this article, we apply to physics the collective predictive coding (CPC), the theory of language/symbol emergence. As our language emerges out of our human communications, physical macroscopic order parameter emerges out of communications among atoms --- each atom is regarded as an agent who predicts each other's behavior through inference. items.title: An upper bound of 60 for the Ramsey number R(3,3,3,3)
items.summary: We improve the upper bound on the classical Ramsey number $R(3,3,3,3)$ from 62 to 60. The proof is based on a global incidence count, classifications of small neighborhoods and exhaustive SAT computations. We formalize the mathematical reductions in Lean and refute every resulting formula with two SAT solvers.

items.summary: We study the relationship between semisimplicity and non-degeneracy for finite-dimensional Hopf triplets over a field of characteristic zero. The non-degeneracy condition appears in the construction of \(4\)-manifold invariants from Hopf triplets, and it was not known whether non-semisimple examples satisfying this condition exist. items.summary: We describe extended interpolation properties of the Katz $p$-adic $L$-function over an imaginary quadratic field. We have three applications. Finally, we prove a large part of the $p$-adic Beilinson conjecture for the Katz $p$-adic $L$-function.

This question is asked and positively answered in recent work of Cadoret-Tamagawa for curves in general, and abelian varieties if the base field has absolute ramification at most $p-1$. items.title: A Winner Classification for Rooted Partizan Edge Geography on Heterogeneous Bouquets of Cycles
items.summary: We consider an undirected edge-traversal game on a finite bouquet of simple cycles. Each of two players controls a token, both tokens begin at the common root, and the players alternate traversing edges that have not been used by either token. A player with no legal move loses. We prove that the first player wins precisely when the number of cycles of odd edge-length is odd, without assuming equal cycle lengths. The proof uses a simultaneous induction on root and defense configurations, with an exact analysis of…

items.title: The Disordered Universe 2025: Analytic Properties of Amplitudes and Correlators
items.summary: These lectures provide an introduction to modern techniques for studying the analytic properties of loop-level scattering amplitudes and correlation functions in perturbative quantum field theory. We begin by developing the ideas behind Landau analysis, which identifies the location and nature of kinematic singularities in Feynman integrals (the universal building blocks that contribute to perturbative amplitudes and correlators). We then show how fundamental principles such as unitarity and causality constrain…

items.title: Learning Multi-Phase Robot Loco-Manipulation via Phase-Conditioned Policy Optimization
items.summary: Complex whole-body loco-manipulation requires executing diverse maneuvers, such as crouching, grasping, and locomotion, within a single long-horizon task. While performing simple pick-and-place behaviors is well-established, scaling to complex, long-horizon tasks remains difficult. Currently, this challenge is addressed by relying on human motion data and correspondingly humanoid platforms, which limits platform independence and introduces substantial data processing overhead. Instead, we extend proximal policy…

items.title: MARQ: A Modular, LLM-Agnostic Requirement Quality Assessor Infused with Systems Engineering Knowledge
items.summary: Requirements engineering (RE) is foundational to systems engineering (SE), as requirement defects can propagate downstream and adversely affect development outcomes. Although large language models (LLMs) are promising for requirement quality assessment, prior work shows that off-the-shelf models miss a large share of expert-identified defects, perform unevenly across quality criteria, and vary across executions. This study investigates whether infusing expert-derived SE knowledge can improve LLM-based requirement…

items.title: Concorde: Geometry-Aware Link Prediction via Decoupled Energy Minimization
items.summary: Link prediction remains difficult in sparse graphs, where diffusion heuristics lack connectivity and geometric methods suffer spectral instability when coupling learned representations with diffusion operators. We introduce Concorde, an energy-based framework that resolves this by decomposing link likelihood into three structurally decoupled branches: (i) a parameter-free spectral anchor that establishes permutation-invariant topological stability; (ii) a mixed-curvature residual on a learnable…

items.title: count-catcher: Lean Theorems from Model Counting Certificates
items.summary: We present count-catcher, a tool that turns a CPOG certificate of a count by the exact model counter d4 into a Lean theorem that a CNF formula defined in Lean has exactly N models over V variables. With an encoding lemma, this theorem becomes a theorem about the number of combinatorial objects. A CPOG certificate consists of a Boolean circuit equivalent to the formula and a proof of equivalence. count-catcher checks in Lean that the formula implies the circuit (forward check) and the circuit implies the formula…

items.title: All Dark Matter as Primordial Black Holes: a Gravitational-Wave Test
items.summary: We propose a novel test for the hypothesis that the dark matter of the Universe is composed entirely by asteroidal-mass primordial black holes. It relies on detecting the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by the coalescence onto rapidly spinning supermassive astrophysical black holes of the light primordial black holes accumulated in spherically symmetric spikes. We discuss the scenarios in which the signal can be observed by the future space-based gravitational-wave observatories LISA and DECIGO.

items.title: Computations in weight 3 of higher Bloch groups
items.summary: We computationally investigate a weight 3 analogue of the relationship between higher Bloch groups, algebraic K-theory, higher regulators, and special values of Dedekind zeta functions. In particular, for F a number field F, we define the pruned Bloch group B _3(F) and compare the covolume of its regulator lattice with zeta_F(3). We define a quantity kappa_3(F), which is conjecturally an integer, that is expected to be closely related to the order of K_4(O_F).

items.title: Landau singularity of the K3 maximal cut in black-hole scattering at fifth post-Minkowskian order
items.summary: Modeling the gravitational waves from merging black holes requires precise calculations of the two-body problem. The post-Minkowskian expansion of black-hole scattering, in powers of Newton's constant, now stands at fifth order, four loops. At this order one part of the deflection diverges when the black holes pass at about 94 percent of the speed of light. The divergence is known to come from periods of a K3 surface, which has a node at this speed. We show that the node lies on the integration contour of the K3…

items.title: Coulomb- and exchange-driven redistribution of spectral correlations
items.summary: Electronic correlations reorganize not only the energies of individual electronic states but also the collective structure of the spectrum. Here, first-principles density functional theory calculations combined with random-matrix spectral statistics are used to examine this reorganization in gamma-Ce within a static spin-polarized DFT+U+SOC description. We distinguish the effects of the Coulomb interaction U from those of the exchange interaction J by analyzing nearest-neighbor spacings, reduced spacing ratios…

items.title: Scaling and Renormalization in Neural Networks: An Effective Renormalization-Group Description of Grokking
items.summary: Grokking is a delayed transition from memorization to generalization in deep neural networks (NNs). We examine whether scaling and renormalization group (RG) theories can describe this dynamics, establishing a quantitative physical framework for neural generalization transitions. For modular addition on a two-layer NN, an ensemble of trained models defines an order parameter (the squared weight norm) and fluctuation proxies for the heat capacity and the susceptibility, with training epoch and weight decay serving…

items.title: Counting Markov triples and simple geodesics
items.summary: We give an asymptotic formula for the number of Markov triples with largest entry below $x$. We show that the error term is $o(\log x)$, which improves upon the previous best known results due to McShane and Rivin. We give an explicit error based on classical zero-free regions of the Riemann zeta function, and a sharper estimate under the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The proof uses the correspondence between Markov triples and simple closed geodesics on the modular punctured torus and a careful analysis of the…

items.title: Axionic Quintessence in Heterotic String Theory
items.summary: We investigate axionic quintessence in heterotic string compactifications. Starting from the ten-dimensional theory, we derive the four-dimensional axion effective action, including gauge couplings and non-perturbative potentials, and identify the curvature terms that can correct it. We examine the geometric requirements for ultralight axions generated by exponentially suppressed worldsheet instantons, finding significant restrictions through an exploratory scan of toric Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces. In an…

items.title: Late reheating in the era of precision cosmology
items.summary: We study the minimum cosmic reheating temperature allowed by recent measurements of primordial nuclear abundances and of the cosmic microwave background. We find that reheating by decays of a light particle into electrons and neutrinos is compatible with both at temperatures around 0.4 MeV, an order of magnitude below the bound for purely electromagnetic channels. This scenario has implications for cosmology and laboratory searches. For example, nearly standard neutrino radiation can coexist with a smaller active…

items.title: Hybrid seesaw from $SU(2)_1 \times SU(2)_2 \times U(1)_Y$
items.summary: We study neutrino mass generation in a model based on the $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_1 \times SU(2)_2 \times U(1)_Y$ gauge symmetry, in which the Standard Model $SU(2)_L$ arises at low energies as the diagonal subgroup of the two $SU(2)$ factors. The symmetry is enlarged with a global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry, spontaneously broken by the vacuum expectation value of a scalar bidoublet. Light neutrino masses are generated at tree level through a hybrid of the type-III, inverse and linear seesaw mechanisms. A distinctive…

items.title: The Harmonic Structure of Multiparticle Scattering: Amplitude Projection and Non-Renormalization
items.summary: We develop a projection formalism for four-dimensional massless scattering amplitudes based on the construction of harmonics on multi-particle phase space. This provides a generalization of the partial-wave decomposition valid for any number of particles. Applying this formalism to calculations of on-shell cuts, we show that any cut calculation can be rewritten as a sum of products of projected coefficients and derive a condition for this sum to vanish. Using the on-shell renormalization group equation in…

items.title: ECH0EZ: Estimating the Hubble constant with ZTF SN Ia DR2
items.summary: Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are instrumental for a precise measurement of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) from the local distance ladder, yet the data used hitherto for this purpose are inhomogeneous and subject to severe selection effects. We present the first, preliminary, cosmological analysis of 772 SNe Ia from the Zwicky Transient Facility's second data release: an untargeted single-telescope sample whose volume-limited subset (z<0.06) is largely free of Malmquist bias. We correct the public data for known…

items.title: Dark Matter Coherent Freeze-Out Mechanism: A Comprehensive Analysis
items.summary: Both Weakly-Interacting Massive Particle (WIMP) and Axion-Like Particle (ALP) are attractive particle dark matter candidates. In this paper we consider a scenario in which both WIMP and ALP are present. The two species interact via a non-derivative quadratic coupling modeled on the axion-nucleon interaction in QCD. We show that even a small (Planck-suppressed) coupling can drastically modify the cosmological history of both species. In the very early Universe, the ALP field acquires a vacuum expectation value…

items.title: Phase Transitions in Mismatched Bayesian Inference for the Ising Model
items.summary: Bayesian inference with a mismatched model can develop an overconfident phase, characterized by posterior agreement without faithful reconstruction of the true state. We study Bayesian inference from noisy bond measurements of an Ising model in its paramagnetic phase, with true inverse temperature $β$ and measurement-noise strength $Δ$, while inference assumes corresponding parameters $β_Q$ and $Δ_Q$. Using replica field theory, we analytically show that the overconfidence phase can occur when inference…

items.title: BPS Chaos and Fortuity in Higgs Branches I: The Gepner Point
items.summary: The BPS states in Calabi-Yau compactifications of type II string theory can sometimes be described using quiver quantum mechanics whose Higgs branch is a complete intersection manifold. Their degeneracy resembles that of BPS black holes. A small fraction of these states corresponds to multi-center supergravity brane configurations and can be continued to the (near-Higgs) Coulomb branch. We identify them as monotone states. The overwhelming majority of states, known as pure-Higgs states, are fortuitous states…

items.title: Can inflationary axion fluctuations dominate over misalignment?
items.summary: The relic abundance of light stable axion dark matter is usually set by misalignment. We study whether the inflationary fluctuations of the axion can dominate instead, and we follow the modes analytically through an instantaneous transition from de Sitter expansion to radiation domination, neglecting the axion mass during inflation and keeping it afterward. Since the energy density is quadratic in the field, a fluctuation-dominated abundance carries an isocurvature perturbation even when the mean displacement…

items.title: The Art of Orbifolding by Huge Non-Abelian Groups
items.summary: We compute torus partition functions of orbifolds of two-dimensional chiral fermions by huge non-Abelian groups involving the Conway group, one of the sporadic finite simple groups. This seemingly standard problem turns out to contain, somewhat unexpectedly, multiple major issues hitherto unresolved, both at the level of the principle and at the level of practice. We describe in detail how they can be overcome. Although the methods described in this paper are generally applicable, the choice of the particular…

items.title: Field-level modeling of halo and galaxy alignments
items.summary: We develop an effective field theory (EFT) of intrinsic alignments at the level of spin-2 field fluctuations of large-scale structure tracers, such as the shapes of galaxies and dark matter halos. Our perturbative model includes the non-linear treatment of the Zel'dovich displacement, and contains all necessary shape operators through the third order. We apply our field-level model to the full 3D distribution of galaxy shapes, whose sky projections are a known contaminant of cosmic shear measurements. Our…

items.title: Stable homotopy theory of higher categories with adjoints
items.summary: We demonstrate that higher categories with adjoints behave like homotopy types. By the homotopy hypothesis, homotopy types can be regarded as higher categories in which all cells are invertible. We show that replacing invertibility by the existence of higher adjoints still supports a homotopy theory that is at least as rich as classical homotopy theory. The basic invariants of this theory are the homotopy monoidal categories \[ Π_n(X,x)=\operatorname{Ho}\bigl(Ω^n(X,x)\bigr) \] associated to a based…

items.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
items.summary: Direct-policy World Action Models (WAM) have demonstrated the benefits of decoupling action generation from explicit future visual prediction for efficient inference in autonomous driving and embodied control. However, they still require tens of denoising steps to achieve competitive action quality, incurring substantial latency and hindering real-time deployment. Simply reducing the number of denoising steps will collapse the nonlinear multi-step denoising trajectory into coarse updates, substantially degrading…

items.title: Improved lattice-packing bounds in small dimensions
items.summary: We strengthen the upper bound on the density of a lattice packing in small dimensions. A lattice cannot have too many short vectors; we modify the Cohn--Elkies linear program accordingly by allowing the auxiliary function to be positive on a short interval beyond the minimum distance. For $11 \leq n \leq 16$, our bound is tighter than the three-point bound of Cohn, de Laat and Salmon. For $n \in [17, 23] \cup [25, 40] \cup [43, 57] \cup [62, 75]\cup [83, 91]$, our bound lies below the published numerical values…

items.title: Parameter-Decoupled Superresolution with Airy-Disk-Informed Learning: Application to NGC 4486B
items.summary: Estimating the separation of two unresolved or nearly unresolved sources from recorded intensity images is difficult when source brightness, mutual coherence, and phase are unknown and the point-spread function (PSF) departs from a Gaussian. We formulate Hermite--Gaussian (HG) projections of one- and two-dimensional Airy amplitudes and prove that ratios of mode probabilities with equal longitudinal parity exactly cancel the brightness, coherence, and phase nuisance parameters under a symmetric two-source model…

items.title: Morse index characterization of the Veronese projective plane
items.summary: Following Simons' seminal work in 1968, every closed, connected, embedded minimal surface in the four-sphere that is not totally geodesic has Morse index at least five. In this paper, we prove that equality holds if and only if the surface is congruent to the Veronese projective plane. Relying on recent advances by Bernstein and Ketover, this characterization settles Kusner's 1996 conjecture on the minimizers of the Willmore functional in dimension four for surfaces whose normal bundle has nonzero Euler number…

items.title: Multimodal Concert Video Editing: System Design and Exploratory Evaluation
items.summary: Editing multi-camera concerts requires coordinated decisions about musical relevance, visual quality and cut timing. We present a modular framework that combines instrument activity from multitrack audio, visible instruments and image sharpness with beat-based timing and probabilistic camera selection. An interpretable scoring model links these components to the choice of views over complete shot intervals. Component tests and an exploratory expert study on a four-camera concert yield mixed assessments across the…

items.title: Parabolic Rectifiable Reifenberg for Measures
items.summary: We announce a structure theory for measures on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic distance. Our results include a parabolic rectifiable Reifenberg theorem for arbitrary Radon measures, qualitative and quantitative characterizations of regular parabolic rectifiability by Jones square functions, and sharp results for $L^p$ beta numbers. The results hold in every parabolic dimension and extend the theories of Edelen--Naber--Valtorta, Azzam--Tolsa and David--Semmes to space-time. The stated…

items.title: Characterising canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties
items.summary: We study Brantner-Taelman's canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties and characterise their (quasi)canonical lifts in terms of rational $p$-adic Hodge theoretic data. We also show that these canonical lifts need not be of CM type and that the associated local Galois representations need not split as sums of twists of unramified representations, in contrast to classical results for abelian varieties and K3 surfaces.

items.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) can generate multiple tokens in parallel, but often require many decoding rounds to complete a response. Efficient generation depends not only on which tokens are easy to predict, but also on how committing to them helps predict the remaining positions. A highly predictable token may provide little useful context, while revealing a less predictable token can help several other positions become predictable sooner. We propose dSpark, a new schedule distillation-based…

items.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
items.summary: Sparse outcome rewards make it difficult for long-horizon language-model agents to assign credit to earlier actions. Learned critics provide value estimates for intermediate states, but these estimates can be inaccurate, while estimating intermediate values with repetitive continuation samples from points within a trajectory incurs substantial costs. To mitigate these issues, we introduce FOCUS, an RL method that uses selective branching to help the critic network learn its value estimator. The rollout controller…

items.title: How to get an attractive model
items.summary: We give a fourth-order Calabi-Yau differential operator, which seems to have been missed by earlier tabulations. We draw attention to this operator because of its clear geometric interpretation and evidence that it possesses a rank-two attractor, conjecturally giving a new example of a Calabi-Yau threefold with modularity properties analogous to those of an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: Persistence Pays: Square-root condition-number dependence for Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin Monte Carlo with a non-reversibly updated accept/reject uniform
items.summary: We prove accelerated mixing for a Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin sampler: the OBABO splitting with friction $2\sqrt m$, adjusted with Neal's non-reversibly updated uniform, which is redrawn after every epoch of $E$ steps. For targets $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $mI\preceq\nabla^2U\preceq LI$ and an $L_H$-Lipschitz Hessian, started from a Gaussian at an approximate minimizer, the chain reaches total variation accuracy $\varepsilon$ after $\tilde O\big(\sqrt{κd}+\sqrt{L_H}(d/m)^{3/4}\big)$ gradient…

items.title: Heavy Heisenberg Algebras, Zero Modes and Modularity
items.summary: It is known due to a result of Miyamoto that zero mode correlators of weight $1$ vectors of vertex operator algebras are quasi-modular forms, and that their generating series are Jacobi forms. In this article we generalize this to higher weight vectors. We consider weight 2 vectors that generate what we call heavy Heisenberg algebras. We prove that their zero mode correlators are a specific type of quasi-modular forms. As a consequence, they too can be summed up into a generating series with Jacobi-like modular…

items.title: Quantifying the failure of symmetry learning in linear diffusion models due to initialization and finite-sample effects
items.summary: Data distributions often possess one or more symmetries: for example, all orientations of any specific dog are included in the distribution of all possible dog pictures. Despite the omnipresence of such symmetries, modern generative modeling approaches may fail to incorporate or learn them, which can lead to lower sample efficiency and poorer generalization. To what extent do diffusion models fail to learn data distribution symmetries, and what sources of symmetry breaking are most responsible? Here, we answer…

items.title: The topological vertex is finitely generated
items.summary: The topological vertex computes all genus amplitudes for the open topological A-model in $\mathbb{C}^3$ with branes on three toric Lagrangians and, via gluing, both open and closed string amplitudes on any toric Calabi-Yau threefold. In this note we show that the topological vertex is generated by boundary interactions of three disks and three annuli. A generalization of this result is shown to hold for the refined topological vertex.

items.title: TrySee: Modular Perception-Enhanced VLM Grounding for Closed-Loop Robot Task Planning in Specialized Domains
items.summary: Vision Language Models (VLMs) have shown impressive capabilities in high-level reasoning and task planning for robots. However, specialized domains remain a challenge for VLMs' image interpretation and grounding abilities. We introduce TrySee, a modular closed-loop robot task planning pipeline integrating general-purpose VLM reasoning with domain-specific perception and established robotics components. The system consists of an inherently reactive cyclic planning pipeline, augmented with domain-specific modular…

items.title: Causal Multiscale Modeling of Ocular FLASH Electroretinography: Model Development, Experimental Fitting, and Spin-Glass--Percolation Predictions
items.summary: Purpose: To develop a causal multiscale model of retinal electroretinography (ERG) after ocular ultrahigh-dose-rate (FLASH) and conventional-dose-rate (CONV) irradiation, evaluate the framework against published ocular ERG data, and derive prospective dose-response predictions for future validation. Methods: The retina was coarse-grained into $N=200$ functional modules. Local rate equations were formulated as Hodgkin--Huxley-inspired conductance-balance/RC reductions of retinal ion-channel and synaptic pathways…

items.title: ArchiveLens: A Generative Spatial Knowledge Framework for Semantic Reconstruction of Historical Maps
items.summary: Historical maps contain dense morphological and semantic information about past urban environments, but many digitization workflows focus primarily on extracting geometry, and do not capture cartographic semantics such as building use and construction materials. This study introduces ArchiveLens, a generative spatial knowledge framework that operationalizes historical maps as entity-centric, machine-queryable geospatial databases. The pipeline decouples morphological and semantic reconstruction through three…

items.title: Modular representations of metabelian groups
items.summary: Let $M$ be a module over a commutative ring with unity $R$, and let $φ:M \to R$ be an $R$-linear map. Then the product $mn = m + (1+φ(m))n$ defines a monoid $Mon(φ)$ on $M$. We show that if $G$ is a group, then $G$ arises as the group of invertible elements of some such monoid $Mon(φ)$ if and only if $G$ is metabelian.

items.title: Curvature-induced fracture mode coupling in doubly curved shells
items.summary: Classical shell fracture theories predominantly consider cracks aligned with principal curvature directions in cylindrical and spherical shells under tensile mode or pressure loading, leaving the fracture behavior of arbitrarily oriented cracks in doubly curved shells under general loading poorly understood. Here, we introduce a semi-analytical framework based on Reissner shallow-shell theory to investigate isotropic shells with positive, zero, and negative Gaussian curvature. The formulation computes stress…

items.title: KAPPA: Checking the Proofs in Statistics Papers with Lean 4 and Language Model Agents
items.summary: Papers in statistical theory rest on long proofs that few readers check line by line. We present KAPPA (Kit of Agents for Proof-checking Papers with a proof Assistant), open-source software that organizes language model agents, run by Claude Code, to translate the proofs of a LaTeX paper into the proof assistant Lean 4 with its library Mathlib and check them there, result by result. Each numbered result receives one of four verdicts: verified unconditionally; verified conditionally, with every cited or unproved…

items.title: Agentic Algorithm Design: LLMs that Propose, Formalise, and Prove Runtime Bounds for Evolutionary Algorithms in Lean
items.summary: LLMs now prove hard theorems in Lean. Can they also design algorithms and prove their correctness and efficiency? LLM-guided design of optimisation heuristics (such as AlphaEvolve) is purely empirical. Automated theorem provers with LLMs prove given statements. So far, there has been little evidence that LLMs can do both: design an algorithm and guarantee its efficiency by a mathematical proof. We present a staged pipeline modelled after research methodology in design and analysis of evolutionary algorithms. The…

items.title: Neutrino Phenomenology and Leptogenesis from Non-Invertible Fusion Symmetry
items.summary: We constructed a minimal type-I seesaw model with two right-handed neutrinos, in which the flavor structure is determined by a non-invertible \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-gauged \(\mathbb{Z}_5\) fusion symmetry~($\mathbb{Z}^{IN}_5$). The framework, incorporating a second Higgs doublet and an auxiliary \(\mathbb{Z}_2\) parity, yields predictive neutrino mass textures without introducing flavon fields. A fit to neutrino data selects the inverted mass ordering with \(m_3=0\) and predicts a nearly maximal Dirac CP phase…

items.title: Relativistic Elastic Scattering of Cosmic-Ray Boosted Dirac Dark Matter with Charged Leptons through a Scalar Mediator
items.summary: We investigate the relativistic kinematics, spinor-recoil structure, and direct-detection phenomenology of a Dirac dark matter fermion interacting with SM charged leptons through a real scalar mediator within a low-energy effective Lagrangian in the fermion mass basis. Standard halo direct-detection searches lose sensitivity for sub-MeV dark matter, because the maximum recoil energy falls below detector thresholds. When halo dark matter particles are upscattered to relativistic energies by galactic cosmic-ray…

items.title: On Hecke algebras at exceptional Eisenstein primes
items.summary: We study the structure over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of the Hecke algebra acting on ordinary cusp forms in the Eisenstein, non-$p$-distinguished case. Our results and methods draw on four complementary approaches: deformation theory, through $R=\mathbf{T}$ theorems; Iwasawa theory, through connections to Sharifi's conjecture; $p$-adic $L$-functions, through an exceptional zero formula; and computational experiments using Magma. We also obtain new results regarding the Coleman--Greenberg conjecture.

items.title: Elastic Scattering of Dirac Dark Matter with Charged Leptons through a Scalar Mediator: Analytical Framework, Numerical Stability, and Direct-Detection Bounds
items.summary: We investigate a leptophilic simplified dark matter model in which a Dirac fermion χinteracts with Standard Model charged leptons \ll through a real scalar mediator S. Starting from the low-energy Yukawa interaction Lagrangian in the fermion mass eigenbasis, we derive closed-form tree-level analytical expressions for the invariant scattering amplitude, the spin-averaged squared matrix element, and the differential and total elastic cross sections. To overcome the numerical loss of significance that arises when…

items.title: On generators and relations for $O_n^irc(V)$ in higher-level Zhu algebras, Part II
items.summary: We study circle relations in the higher-level Zhu algebra of a vertex operator algebra $V$. For regular vacuum words in homogeneous letters, we prove the termwise correction-residue conjecture of Part I: every correction in the one-sided iterate expansion belongs separately to the finite-length plus subspace. The first correction formed with the left truncated field vanishes identically. Multiplying the diagonal commutator kernel by a power of $1+x$ turns it into a Laurent polynomial. This proves the vanishing…

items.title: Negative-Power Density of States in Chiral-Orthogonal Disordered Systems and the IR Phase of QCD
items.summary: The recently discovered IR phase of QCD is characterized by an infrared (IR) sector of Dirac modes that separates and dynamically decouples from the bulk of the spectrum, becoming scale invariant in the process [1]. Among key features of this IR sector is the negative power-law behavior of Dirac spectral density near zero with power close to $-1$. Here we start investigating to what extent can this behavior be mimicked by chiral Anderson models. In particular, we study 3-D chiral-orthogonal systems with…

items.title: Existence of a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations enjoying the energy equality
items.summary: To date, a Leray's weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations enjoys an energy inequality. We prove the existence of a weak solution that enjoys the energy equality. The existence of the weak solution is achieved as limit of solutions to the mollified Navier-Stokes system (Leray's approach). Since no uniqueness result is known for weak solutions we are not able to claim that any weak solution in the sense of Leray-Hopf enjoys the energy equality.

items.title: Model-independent calibration of gamma-ray bursts with Bayesian neural networks
items.summary: Context. Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) extend cosmological distance measurements beyond the range densely sampled by Type Ia supernovae, but their standardization requires reliable calibration and uncertainty estimates. Aims. We calibrate the Amati correlation without assuming a background cosmological model, assess its stability, and examine the cosmological reach of current and future GRB Hubble diagrams. Methods. We train a Bayesian neural network on Pantheon+ supernovae, assess and recalibrate its predictive…

items.title: TP-JSCC: Efficient Token Pruning and Joint Source-Channel Coding for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration
items.summary: Deploying large vision-language models (LVLMs) on resource-constrained embodied agents for 3D visual question answering necessitates cloud-edge collaboration. However, offloading massive visual data to the cloud over bandwidth-limited and noisy channels introduces severe latency and transmission distortion. To address this, we propose TP-JSCC, an efficient token pruning and joint source-channel coding method for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration. items.title: Parameter-Decoupling-Informed Learning for Superresolution: Laboratory Validation and Galaxy Imaging
items.summary: We present a parameter-decoupling-informed learning model for estimating subwavelength separations of point sources, without requiring prior knowledge of source properties, control over the sources, or continued access to their light signals. The method builds on our parameter-decoupled quantum superresolution estimation theory, which circumvents the need to estimate nuisance parameters such as partial coherence, brightness imbalance, and relative phase. Our convolutional neural network further accommodates…

items.title: Probing the singlet-triplet scotogenic model with lepton flavor violation, gravitational waves and dark matter
items.summary: We perform a comprehensive phenomenological analysis of neutrino masses, lepton-flavor violation, gravitational-wave signature induced by the first-order electroweak phase transition, and scalar dark matter within the framework of the singlet--triplet scotogenic model. We derive general analytical expressions for the one-loop Wilson coefficients of the penguin and box contributions to lepton-flavor-violating processes, considering generic scalar and fermion mediators. items.title: Boundary Layer Criterion for the Low Mach Number and Inviscid Limits in Compressible Fluid-Rigid Body Interaction
items.summary: We investigate the simultaneous low Mach number and vanishing viscosity limit for a three-dimensional compressible viscous fluid interacting with a freely moving rigid body. The fluid satisfies the compressible Navier-Stokes equations and the no-slip condition on the body surface, while the body evolves according to Newton's laws driven by the fluid stresses. items.title: Skill$^\infty$: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Skill Optimization
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI), in which a system also improves the way it improves, is a long-standing aspiration on the path to AGI. Language agents increasingly store procedural knowledge in reusable skills. Optimizing skills offers a direct way to achieve RSI, because the optimization procedure itself can be encoded as a skill. Existing skill optimizers, however, follow a hand-designed procedure. Even methods that evolve a meta-skill confine it to a fixed pipeline and relearn it for each task. We present…

items.title: Microscopic Derivation of Stochastic Thin-Film Equation and Extensions to Two-Layer and Evaporating Films
items.summary: While classical thin-film hydrodynamics models widely govern macroscopic fluid layers, they fail to capture the molecular-level thermal fluctuations that dictate nanoscale interfacial dynamics. Standard stochastic extensions rely on the long-wave approximation of the continuum fluctuating Navier-Stokes equations; however, this top-down paradigm lacks a formal connection to microscopic particle trajectories and cannot readily accommodate complex, non-equilibrium boundary mechanisms. items.title: A framework for trackable and modular rounding error analysis
items.summary: Robust and meaningful rounding error analysis is becoming increasingly challenging as modern numerical computations involve a rapidly evolving variety of arithmetic formats, precisions, and computational kernels. We propose a trackable and modular framework for rounding error analysis, together with a new notation for bounding accumulated rounding errors. items.summary: We propose fast-spinning, magnetic white dwarfs in binary systems as promising sources of continuous gravitational waves for future space-based detectors. Motion along these directions changes gauge couplings, the QCD scale, quark masses, and Yukawa parameters. A given string-derived sector then predicts low-energy slopes. items.title: Invariance in half-space last passage percolation and directed polymers
items.summary: We prove various invariance properties for half-space geometric and exponential last passage percolation and the half-space log-gamma polymer, analogous to the full-space invariances proved by Dauvergne. We use the RSK and geometric RSK correspondences to establish a conditional distributional identity between the half-space models and the corresponding full-space models, which allows us to directly transfer the invariance results in the full space to the half space.

items.summary: The orbital evolution of a neutron star and a much lower-mass primordial black hole can differ strikingly from that of typical compact binaries. Dynamical tides, analogous to those in the Solar System's giant planet-moon systems, can accelerate inspiral or induce outspiral, depending on the orbital configuration. items.summary: Storage-disaggregated databases decouple compute from storage, improving elasticity but suffering from network bottlenecks. Most cloud databases use page-based B+trees and buffer pools. Under disaggregation, each index traversal incurs serial network round-trips. Page-granularity transfers and caching also amplify network traffic and lower cache efficiency. items.title: On the evenness of coefficients of modular forms
items.summary: We study the density of primes such that $a_p$ is divisible by a prime above $2$ for modular forms $f = \sum_{n \ge 1} a_n q^n$ of small levels. First, we reduce the problem to low weight and odd level, or a mod $2$ CM type form. Then, we provide calculations for the evenness of particular newforms. In particular, we provide a list of levels where this "evenness" can be computed exactly for all the forms with trivial nebentypus.

items.title: On the Upsilon invariant and the Baldwin-Vela-Vick b-invariant of fibered knots
items.summary: For a null-homologous fibered knot $K$ in a rational homology sphere, Baldwin and Vela-Vick define a refinement $b(K)$ of the Ozsváth-Szabó contact invariant. items.title: A unified and composable framework for modeling packed-bed liquid chromatography
items.summary: Packed-bed chromatography is a cornerstone of bioseparation, yet its modeling landscape remains fragmented by numerous model variants, inconsistent terminology, and limited structural clarity. While prior work has categorized and contrasted individual variants, our approach shifts the focus to unification. items.summary: Classical optimization and learning-guided search offer complementary approaches to open problems in discrete mathematics, but their outputs are difficult to compare when search spaces, validity checks, and stopping rules differ. We present \emph{RadonBench}, a benchmark for constructing maximum-cardinality Radon-free lattice configurations: finite subsets of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ admitting no integral Radon partition. items.summary: Today, data center networks run multiple congestion control algorithms (CCAs), each tailored to distinct traffic characteristics, from latency-sensitive intra-region RPCs to high-throughput cross-region AI workloads. items.summary: Wireless underground sensor networks (WUSNs) enable in-situ monitoring of subsurface processes and buried assets to deliver substantial social and economic benefits across diverse verticals. We establish the existence of universal $p$-adic power series whose evaluations, together with their compatible $p$-power roots, generate perfectoidizations of ideals. In the special case of the perfectoidization of $\mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/p^{\infty}}\rangle/(t-1)$, we describe a linear…

items.title: Towards $al N=8$ Supergravity in $al N=1$ Superspace
items.summary: We study the possibility of constructing maximally supersymmetric supergravity in ${\cal N}=1$ superspace. We dimensionally reduce the eleven dimensional supersymmetry transformations, and decouple these transformations using the residual $G_2$ symmetry of the theory. This allows us to find the ${\cal N}=1$ superfields relevant to this theory. Among our results, we find a description of a self-dual superfield involving a spin 1 and a spin 3/2 field which does not seem to have been discussed previously in the…

items.title: Sharp Bounds on the Winner's Bias under Independent and Nonnegatively Correlated Noise
items.summary: Reporting the best of $M$ noisy, unbiased scores overstates the winner's value by up to $c\sqrt{V}$, where $V$ is the total noise variance and the sharp constant $c$ depends on how the noise is dependent. It was known only at the two extremes, arbitrary dependence ($\sqrt{(M-1)/M}$) and i.i.d. noise. items.title: Robotic Budding: From Homogeneous Cells to Diverse Morphologies in Physical Self-Reproduction
items.summary: Physical self-reproduction in modular robots remains difficult because a robot must not only move, but also collect, align, dock, and separate modules reliably in hardware. Taking inspiration from how genetically identical cells form the varied tissues of an organism, we introduce a single standardized robotic module that combines a magnetic docking interface with two actuated joints and folds from a flat, two-dimensional configuration into three-dimensional structures. Modules of this single design can be…

items.title: Elliptic curve rank growth in multi-quadratic extensions
items.summary: In this article we give an algorithm to produce infinitely many explicit quadratic twists of a given elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ with a rational point and fixed root number. Moreover, under the Parity Conjecture (or other technical hypotheses), for each $n\geq 1$, we produce explicit multi-quadratic extensions $L_n$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, of degree $2^n$, such that the growth in rank from $\mathbb{Q}$ to $L_n$ is at least $\max\{2n+2^{n-1}-1,\,2^n-1\}$ when the root number of $E$ is $-1$, and at least…

items.title: Finite-distance effects and scalar suppression in massive gravity
items.summary: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) probe the stochastic gravitational wave (GW) background through the angular cross-correlations of timing residuals. For a GW background in general relativity (GR), the expected overlap reduction function (ORF) is given by the Hellings--Downs (HD) correlation. We investigate how a nonzero graviton mass modifies this prediction through a massive dispersion relation and additional vector and scalar polarizations, producing a modified effective ORF. In the massive limit, the…

items.title: Polarized Ensemble Kalman Inversion: A Derivative-Free Method for Multimodal Inverse Problems with Non-asymptotic Analysis
items.summary: Inverse problems often admit multiple solutions consistent with the same noisy, indirect observations, especially with sparse data and/or strongly nonlinear forward models. Ensemble Kalman inversion (EKI) provides a robust, derivative-free framework to solve inverse problems, but its global empirical covariances couple all ensemble members across distinct solution modes, limiting its effectiveness for multimodal problems. We introduce polarized ensemble Kalman inversion (PEKI), which constructs distance-weighted…

items.title: Real-to-Sim Calibration of Bosch Etching Simulators with Few-Shot XSEM Data and Hybrid Search
items.summary: The Bosch process is widely used in MEMS and TSV fabrication, but accurate prediction of etching outcomes remains difficult without calibration against real measurements, which are sparse and costly to obtain. This work presents a few-shot real-to-sim calibration framework that decouples simulator parameters from direct process variables to infer a recipe-specific simulator parameter vector from sparse measurements, enabling reliable prediction of etch depth and sidewall angle under held-out process conditions…

items.title: Distributed Swarm Morphogenesis with Neural Cellular Automata
items.summary: Swarm morphogenesis requires robots to assemble desired shapes through local interactions. We present a modular framework integrating neural cellular automata (NCA) with existing site assignment and collision-aware control. Within this framework, we introduce a decentralized attachment-site discovery mechanism. Robots already in the formation update and share local NCA states to identify new attachment sites, enabling progressive growth without a predefined list of sites during deployment. To bridge the mismatch…

items.title: Scaling Transformer Energy-based Models For High Quality Image Synthesis
items.summary: Energy-Based Models (EBMs) are a flexible class of generative models that decouple probabilistic modeling from the generation process. This decoupling directly enables compositional generation and inference-time scaling, where sample quality can be refined simply by increasing sampling steps. However, severe challenges in high-dimensional sampling and training instabilities with deep architectures have restricted EBMs to low-dimensional regimes. To resolve these bottlenecks, we introduce the Transformer…

items.title: A frame-indifferent rank-one convex function in three dimensions which is not quasiconvex
items.summary: We construct a function $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times3}\to\mathbb{R}$ which is frame-indifferent, $W(QF)=W(F)$ for all $Q\in\mathrm{SO}(3)$, rank-one convex, but not quasiconvex. In a neighbourhood of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ the function is an explicit polynomial of degree four in the strain $F^TF-\mathrm{Id}$; the failure of quasiconvexity occurs at $F=\mathrm{Id}$ through a third-order mechanism of Šverák type, with test functions whose gradients are arbitrarily close to $\mathrm{Id}$. The polynomial is obtained from a…

items.title: Semi-Analytic Predictions for Strong-Lensing Perturbers in Cold and Self-Interacting Dark Matter
items.summary: Strong gravitational lensing is sensitive to the abundance and internal structure of dark matter halos, providing a probe of gravothermal evolution in self-interacting dark matter (SIDM). We combine semi-analytic cold dark matter (CDM) subhalo histories with a model for gravothermal evolution in SIDM to generate CDM and SIDM subhalo populations across SIDM parameter space. We predict their projected enclosed masses and deflection-based projected density slopes and compare them with three perturbers inferred…

items.title: A localisation bound for Standard-Model representations in heterotic orbifolds
items.summary: In heterotic string compactifications on toroidal orbifolds, the massless states at a twisted fixed point are constrained by the evenness of the sixteen-dimensional gauge lattice. We show that two massless left-chiral states in the same Standard-Model representation, built on the same constructing space-group element and distinct modulo the Weyl group of $SU(3)_c\times SU(2)_L$, must satisfy $\sqrt{R}+\sqrt{R'}\ge\sqrt{2}$, where $R$ is the squared length of the part of a state's gauge momentum orthogonal to the…

items.title: Quantitative nodal domain count for Maass forms
items.summary: We consider a real even Hecke-Maass cusp form $φ$ on the modular surface, with Laplace eigenvalue $1/4+T^2$. We prove that its restriction to any fixed compact segment $β$ of the vertical geodesic above $i$ has $\gg_{β,\varepsilon} T^{1/6-\varepsilon}$ sign changes, yielding the same lower bound for the number of distinct inert nodal domains meeting the segment. items.title: IFC-SSL-Bench: Benchmarking Self-Supervised Learning for Annotation-Efficient Multispectral Imaging Flow Cytometry
items.summary: Imaging Flow Cytometry (IFC) generates large multispectral datasets, yet the need for expert annotations bottlenecks the development of supervised deep learning models. While Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) offers a solution, its application to IFC remains fragmented and lacks systematic benchmarking. To address this, we present IFC-SSL-Bench, a modular framework for evaluating SSL in IFC. We benchmark six SSL approaches across four backbones on two heterogeneous datasets. By assessing downstream classification…

items.title: The Calabi-Yau and Sullivan conjectures for minimal surfaces with symmetries
items.summary: Let \(G\) be a finite group acting on a connected open Riemann surface \(X\) by holomorphic automorphisms and acting on a Euclidean space \(\mathbb R^n\), \(n\ge 3\), by orthogonal transformations. In a previous paper, the second author gave a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a \(G\)-equivariant conformal minimal immersion \(F:X\to\mathbb R^n\), and he asked whether such \(F\) can be chosen to be a proper map. Assuming that this condition holds, we give an affirmative answer when \(X\) is a…

items.title: SAGE: A hybrid vision-language and geometry framework for work-zone pathway prediction under temporary traffic control
items.summary: Temporary traffic control redirects vehicles through work zones, requiring automated vehicles to connect an interpretation of the visible devices to a continuous passing path. Geometric predictors provide several plausible paths, yet selecting the one consistent with the temporary control remains difficult. We propose SAGE (Semantic-to-Action Grounded Execution), a read-decide-execute-check framework that separates path construction, path preference, and control compliance within a shared candidate space. The…

items.title: Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson classes of symmetric powers and applications
items.summary: The Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson class $c_{SM}(X)$ is defined in the Chow group $A_*(X)$ of a scheme $X$, and generalizes $c(T_X)\cap [X]$ if $X$ is smooth. In this paper we independently compute $c_{SM}(S^nX)\in A_*(S^nX)$ modulo $n!$ torsion; we use this result to compute the pushforward to $S^nX$ of $c_{SM}(Quot^n_X(E))$ (and in particular $c_{SM}(Hilb^n X)$) when $X$ is smooth and $E$ is a vector bundle on $X$. items.title: PaperFormalizer: Author-in-the-Loop Autoformalization of Research Papers in Lean
items.summary: Even a carefully proofread paper can leave small gaps in its proofs or its stated assumptions. We introduce PaperFormalizer, a Lean-based agentic pipeline that helps authors find and close such gaps in their own papers and turn each paper into a Lean-verified version. Starting from the LaTeX source, PaperFormalizer transcribes the paper into a dependency graph of statements, audits each statement in natural language for faithfulness, ambiguity and correctness, and then formalizes and proves the statements in Lean…

items.title: Rapid stabilization for Stokes and Navier-Stokes systems with localized disturbance
items.summary: In this study, we analyze the rapid stabilization of Stokes and the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems in the presence of an unknown spatially localized disturbance. A multivalued feedback control strategy is proposed which combines the Lyapunov frequency method with the multivalued sign operator. This methodology connects Lyapunov-based stability analysis with spectral inequalities, while the inclusion of the sign operator provides robustness against disturbance. items.title: Ozone groups and centers of two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras
items.summary: Let $p,q$ be roots of unity with $pq\neq1$, and put $\ell=|\langle p,q\rangle|$ and $t=\ord(pq)$. Up to isomorphism, the two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras $\mathcal H_{p,q}$ are exactly the noetherian PI graded down-up algebras, so everything here holds for that whole class. The ozone group is $μ_\ell\timesμ_{\ell/t}$, generated by conjugation by three normal elements, and the center is recovered from the fixed ring of the ozone group as the invariants of a cyclic group of order $t$. items.title: Relative Langlands duality for linear periods
items.summary: We prove relative Langlands duality for $X = GL_{p+q}/(GL_p \times GL_q)$. These symmetric spaces arise in the setting of the linear period of Friedberg-Jacquet when $p=q$, and exhibit non-tempered behavior when $q>p+1$. Via the real-symmetric correspondence, we establish a derived Satake equivalence for the real group $G_{\mathbb R}=U(p,q)$, and use it to obtain a constructible realization of coherent sheaves on Kato's exotic nilpotent cones. items.title: Flavored $S_{3}$ Non-Minimal Left-Right Symmetric Model
items.summary: In this work we investigate fermion masses and flavor mixings in a non-minimal left-right symmetric model endowed with the non-Abelian discrete symmetry $S_3$. The scalar sector contains three Higgs bidoublets, while one left-handed and one right-handed triplet generate Majorana neutrino masses. Assigning the first two fermion families to an $S_3$ doublet and the third family to a singlet, together with a specific alignment of the bidoublet vacuum expectation values, leads to a common and analytically tractable…

items.title: Gauge It or Break It: Lectures on Global Symmetries and the Cobordism Conjecture
items.summary: These lecture notes introduce the No Global Symmetries Conjecture in the context of the Swampland Program, with particular emphasis on the Cobordism Conjecture. We begin with a review of ordinary and higher-form symmetries, their realization by extended operators, and mechanisms for gauging or breaking them. We then discuss the no global symmetries principle, including evidence from black hole physics, string perturbation theory, and AdS/CFT, and its relation to other Swampland constraints. A central theme is the…

items.title: Ricci flow of Integrable Sigma Models, Hitchin Systems and Quantum Seiberg-Witten theory
items.summary: We construct a family of integrable 2d sigma models through 4d Chern-Simons theory and show that their classical point-particle reduction corresponds to a Hitchin system. The integrable Hitchin quantisation then provides a natural candidate Hamiltonian for the one-loop reduced dynamics of the sigma models, which coincides with the Perelman operator in all cases examined.
