items.title: Global Convergence and Reliable Stopping in a Safeguarded Modified Anderson--Björck Method
items.summary: The modified Anderson-Bjorck (modAB) method was first proposed in 2023 by Ganchovski and Traykov for solving nonlinear equations in structural mechanics. It was improved further in 2026 by introducing better switching criteria with account to function symmetry, and bisection fallback based on measuring the bracket reduction rate. Although the algorithm demonstrated superior performance across a great variety of functions, it lacked formal mathematical analysis and proof of convergence. In addition, some…

items.title: Gauss-Manin Connection in Disguise: Holomorphic Anomaly Equations and Higher Genus Real Gromov-Witten Invariants
items.summary: We construct an algebraic framework for the extended holomorphic anomaly equations following ideas of Alim, Movasati, Scheidegger and Yau. We choose the quintic threefold as our main model and use this framework to solve the equations and fix the ambiguity up to genus 5. We obtain predictions for real Gromov-Witten invariants, or, equivalently, real Gopakumar-Vafa invariants that are integers and agree with their complex counterparts modulo 2. In the end, we discuss how the framework could be extended and compute…

items.title: Collider and direct detection as key probes of asymmetric dark matter: Signals from a compressed Inert Higgs doublet
items.summary: The cosmic imbalance of particles over antiparticles may be inherited by the dark matter in a certain class of asymmetric dark matter models. In this article, we thoroughly investigate the signatures of the minimal realization of this idea. In this model a new (stable) inert Higgs, $H'$, plays the role of the mediator that facilitates the asymmetry transfer from the visible to the dark sector. It also constitutes a small dark matter sub-component, while the dominant component stems from a singlet scalar…

items.title: Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite
items.summary: In the abelian sandpile model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, a site with at least $2d$ grains topples by sending one grain to each neighbor. In a box $[-N,N]^d$ whose boundary absorbs grains, adding grains at random sites and toppling defines a Markov chain. Athreya and Járai (2004) constructed the stationary state on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ as the limit of its stationary distributions as $N\to\infty$. They asked whether, when a grain is added at the origin of a sandpile in the stationary state, the resulting avalanche of topplings…

items.title: The Tate Conjecture for Ordinary Calabi-Yau Threefolds
items.summary: We use the theory of canonical lifts to prove the integral geometric Tate conjecture for ordinary Calabi-Yau threefolds over finite fields, and also for divisor classes on certain ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties.

items.title: The Haagerup VOA at $c=8$
items.summary: We announce an explicit construction of a unitary, strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge $8$ inside $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$, with a ribbon equivalence $\mathrm{Rep}(U)\simeq Z(\mathcal H_3)$ realizing the Haagerup double. The vertex algebra is generated by six affine currents and three specified weight-two fields; its weight-one Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2$, at levels $1$ and $39$. We outline the argument, which combines exact lattice calculations, an all-weight…

items.title: Reflected entropy and islands in JT gravity from partial dimensional reduction
items.summary: We study how mixed-state correlations reorganize across island transitions in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity coupled to a non-gravitating bath. Using the partial-dimensional-reduction realization of double holography, we compute reflected entropy for adjacent and disjoint radiation regions in the vacuum and in the thermofield-double state of an eternal black hole. Reflected entropy probes the internal partition of the entanglement wedge and therefore resolves structure that is invisible to the ordinary Page curve: its…

items.title: The Inviscid Limit in Uniformly Local Yudovich Spaces
items.summary: We consider solutions to the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes and Euler equations with the velocity in $L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and the vorticity in the uniformly local Yudovich space $Y^θ_{ul}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We show that if $θ$ grows sufficiently slowly, then for every $T>0$, solutions of the Navier-Stokes equation converge to solutions of the Euler equation in $L^{\infty}([0,T];L^2_{ul}(\mathbb{R}^2))$ as $ν\to 0^+$, provided they are generated from the same initial data.

items.title: A Lean Formalization of the Hamilton--Perelman Proof of Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture
items.summary: We formalize the Hamilton--Perelman Ricci-flow proof of Thurston's geometrization conjecture. The public Lean declaration is reproduced in this paper. Its geometric interpretation follows, and verification is recorded in 4.

items.title: Clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers: spectral bounds and anticodes
items.summary: Using spectral and polynomial methods, we show several sharp spectral bounds for the clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers that only use spectral information from the original graph. In particular, we strengthen earlier spectral-radius estimates to obtain an asymptotically sharp colouring bound for general graph powers, and prove a sharp bound for powers of line graphs with a complete characterisation of equality. We also develop polynomial methods yielding upper and lower bounds for clique numbers of…

items.title: Weighted, GIT and Néron--Tate heights on genus-two moduli and Jacobians
items.summary: We compare three heights attached to a curve of genus two: the weighted height of its Igusa--Clebsch invariants, the GIT height of a binary sextic defining it, and the Néron--Tate height on its Jacobian. For a morphism from an abelian variety to a weighted projective space we define a weighted Néron--Tate height and show that the weighted height differs from it by a linear form and a bounded function; the linear form vanishes when inversion is induced by an automorphism of the weighted projective space. For…

items.title: Relaxation Dark Energy: Compositional Dynamics and the Future of Cosmic Acceleration
items.summary: If cosmic acceleration is driven by a positive cosmological constant, the universe approaches an eternally accelerating de Sitter state, whose interpretation in quantum gravity remains elusive. We develop a framework in which acceleration is instead a transient stage of dark-sector relaxation towards compositional equilibrium: matter and dark energy approach a stationary density ratio, eventually diluting like pressureless matter. Guided by linear response theory and Onsager's near-equilibrium regression…

items.title: $f(Q,T)$ Gravity with Barrow Holographic Dark Energy and Massive Neutrinos: DESI DR2 Constraints and Implications for the Hubble Tension
items.summary: We study a modification of symmetric teleparallel gravity in which the function $f(Q,T)$ is linear in the non-metricity scalar $Q$ and the trace $T$ of the energy-momentum tensor, combined with a Barrow holographic dark energy (BHDE) density built from the Granda-Oliveros infrared cutoff. The resulting background equations are solved in a modified version of \texttt{hi\_class} and constrained with Pantheon+ supernovae, 32 cosmic chronometer $H(z)$ points, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, and Planck 2018 CMB…

items.title: Shear-driven arrest of dip-coating film entrainment
items.summary: A plate withdrawn from a bath of partially wetting liquid entrains a film above a critical velocity. Here, we show that this critical threshold can be substantially increased by the presence of a laminar gas flow opposed to the plate velocity that exerts a tangential shear stress on the liquid-gas interface. Using two-phase immiscible Navier-Stokes simulations and confining the gas to a narrow channel, we derive a closed-form expression for the interfacial stress, which combined with lubrication theory relates…

items.title: Transformer-based In-Context Score Operator Learning for Diffusion Models
items.summary: Diffusion models typically learn the generative dynamics of a single target distribution or a family of distributions indexed by conditioning variables fixed during training. This limits their ability to adapt to a previously unseen distribution from only a small set of examples. We introduce an in-context solution operator learning framework for diffusion models, in which each target distribution is treated as a task drawn from a meta-distribution and is specified at inference time by an empirical context set…

items.title: The Renormalized Area--Willmore Relation
items.summary: In [1, Proposition 8.1], Alexakis and Mazzeo showed that the renormalized area of minimal surfaces in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^3$ approaching the ideal boundary $\partial_\infty\mathbb{H}^3$ is the negative of the Willmore energy of their Euclidean conformal compactifications. In this paper, we investigate whether there are other geometric surface equations for which these two quantities satisfy a universal proportionality relation. We answer this question in the affirmative by extending the…

items.title: Regularization of a Divergent Arithmetic Product via the Asymptotic Monoid: The Case of $(-1)^{ω(n)}$
items.summary: We apply the generalized monoid of words and logarithmic-prefix functionals of \cite{C1} to the regularization of the divergent product \[ P_ω=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{(-1)^{ω(n)}}, \] where \(ω(n)\) is the number of distinct prime divisors of \(n\). The associated Dirichlet series \(D_ω(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{ω(n)}n^{-s}\) has a natural boundary at \(\Re(s)=0\), as established by Meretov (1987) and recovered here as a special case of the Estermann--Dahlquist theory of Euler products, which makes zeta regularization…

items.title: Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving with Solve, Review, Wiki, Verify
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly improving on long-horizon scientific and olympiad tasks. Recent systems have produced a Lean-formalized resolution of the Navier--Stokes problem and autonomous solutions to four open questions in the Erdős Conjectures database. Yet neither system releases both its underlying model and complete inference stack. More broadly, a single agent session remains brittle on difficult problems: early errors can propagate, missing domain knowledge can stall progress, and…

items.title: Global Existence of Strong and Weak Solutions to the 2D Compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson System in Bounded Domains with Large Data and Vacuum
items.summary: We study the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson system in a general simply connected bounded domain with Navier-slip boundary conditions and a positive, possibly non-flat, doping profile. We establish the global existence of a unique strong solution and of a global weak solution for arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum when the shear viscosity is a positive constant and the bulk one proportional to a power of the density with the power bigger than 4/3. The main difficulties arise from…

items.title: Global Existence and Partial Regularity for the Three-Dimensional Chemotaxis--Navier--Stokes System in a Half-Space
items.summary: We establish endpoint partial regularity for suitable weak solutions to the three-dimensional chemotaxis--Navier--Stokes system with constant sensitivity and linear consumption in a half-space under no-slip and no-flux boundary conditions. The full space--time singular set, including its boundary part, has vanishing one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure. This follows from a Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg type criterion at the natural $r^{-1}$ dissipation scaling, valid at interior and boundary points without…

items.title: zip2zip++: Towards Inference-Time Token Compression with Minimal Quality Loss
items.summary: Dynamic vocabularies built on-the-fly via Lempel-Ziv-Welch (LZW) compression let a language model represent the same text in fewer tokens, but prior work shows that this efficiency comes at a cost to reasoning and perplexity. We show that this quality gap is not a fundamental price of compression but can be substantially closed through targeted improvements to the compression layer and LZW codec, without modifying the underlying pretrained language model. Our analysis reveals four key issues: (1) LZW's…

items.title: Diverging paths to dark-matter discovery
items.summary: The scientific discovery of dark matter has been pursued in two very different methodological and epistemic contexts. A microphysical context centered around the laboratory detection of a new particle, and a macrophysical context based on the astronomical identification of a non-luminous gravitating component. The justification for the salience of methodological diversity is that these different methods are complementary ways to discovering aspects of the same entity. The weakly interacting massive particle…

items.title: On the Cohomology Classes of Certain Eisenstein-Kronecker Forms
items.summary: We study the de Rham cohomology and Deligne splitting for a class of Eisenstein-Kronecker forms by introducing a modular weight grading. As an application, we compute a particular cohomology class that gives rise to generating series of Gromov-Witten invariants of elliptic curves.

items.title: Appell Sequences in Analytic Number Theory: Shifted Expansions and Dirichlet L-Functions
items.summary: We place the Appell shift theorem for asymptotic expansions inside a Borel--Laplace framework and apply it to two classical functions of analytic number theory: the Hurwitz zeta function \(ζ(m,q)\) and the Lerch transcendent \(Φ(z,m,a)\). The resulting shifted expansions have coefficients given by Appell polynomials evaluated at the shift, with remainders controlled uniformly on compact sets. The generating sequences are identified explicitly in terms of the Taylor coefficients of the Borel kernels. In a second…

items.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Finslerian Cosmological Dark Energy Model
items.summary: Modified extensions of the standard cosmological models often introduce complex parameter degeneracies that severely impact sampling convergence of the parameter space while analyzing the model observationally. In this work, we present an accelerated Bayesian inference technique using a Heteroscedastic Deep Ensemble with Monte Carlo Dropout incorporating distance-gated local residual corrections to emulate complex likelihood surfaces and avoid extrapolation beyond the trained region. We demonstrate this…

items.title: The School on Gravity: from motion to commotion
items.summary: Understanding the gravitational interaction is one of the great scientific endeavors of the 21st century. The Nobel Prize-winning discovery of gravitational waves in 2015, and subsequent detections by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration, have marked a revolutionary step forward in physics and astrophysics by opening an entirely new window for exploring the Universe. Future upgrades to these detectors, along with upcoming facilities such as LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and radio and optical instruments, promise…

items.title: Two Cosmological Histories in a New Exponential Infrared $f(T)$ Teleparallel Gravity: Implications for the Hubble Tension and the Low-$\ell$ Planck TT--EE Tension
items.summary: We investigate a particular case of the New Exponential Infrared $f(T)$ teleparallel gravity model with the same number of free parameters as the standard $Λ$CDM model. Remarkably, due to the two real branches of the Lambert function $W$, the model admits two distinct cosmological solutions, denoted by $f^{(I)}$CDM and $f^{(II)}$CDM. The former exhibits a late-time phantom crossing, whereas the latter predicts an effective dark-energy density evolving from negative to positive values. Using a Markov Chain Monte…

items.title: Exact rational certificates and a Lean formalization of the eleven-variable Vasc inequality
items.summary: We prove that the cyclic sum $\sum_{i=0}^{10}(x_i-x_{i+1})/(x_{i+1}+x_{i+2})$ is nonnegative for every strictly positive real eleven-tuple, with indices taken modulo eleven. Clearing denominators reduces the problem to a homogeneous polynomial. Subtracting the smallest coordinate then separates the proof into nonnegativity of a common-translation derivative and nonnegativity on a full boundary face. We supply exact rational polynomial certificates in Gram-matrix form for both statements. The derivative…

items.title: Non intrusive parametric Reduced Order Models based on physics for incompressible flow
items.summary: Reduced order modeling provides an efficient alternative to high fidelity simulations for the rapid prediction of fluid flows in many query settings. Among non intrusive approaches, Operator Inference (OpInf) enables the identification of reduced dynamical operators directly from data while preserving a prescribed mathematical structure. The present work extends physics structured OpInf to the construction of parametric Reduced Order Models for transient incompressible flows governed by the Navier-Stokes…

items.title: Recovering a Riemannian manifold from minimal surface areas
items.summary: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold from the areas of minimal surfaces. We show that areas of minimal surfaces determine the metric on manifolds foliated by minimal surfaces, up to boundary-fixing isometry. This resolves the conjecture on boundary rigidity for least-area data in an exterior formulation, even without topological restrictions on the minimal surfaces. We also prove global rigidity for Einstein metrics on compact three-manifolds with boundary, assuming $\(π_1(M,\partial…

items.title: Short Recurrences and Straight-Line Programs for Primes
items.summary: We give a short autonomous recurrence that generates every odd prime, in increasing order, from the single initial value $8$. Its integer state determines both its output and its next update: the lowest set bit gives the next prime, while the highest set bit determines the sieve period. The same state also determines the following prime gap. A related recurrence represents the prime-counting function as the $2$-adic valuation of a single integer. Independently, a direct packing of a finite divisor sieve yields…

items.title: Probing generalized equation of state for dark energy with latest cosmological probes
items.summary: Baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements from DESI DR2 have strengthened indications of a time-evolving dark energy. In this paper, we investigate observational constraints on the generalized equation of state (GEoS) for dark energy, $w(a) = w_0 - w_β(a^β- 1)/β$, with latest data from UV and X-ray observations of high-redshift quasars, DESI DR2 BAO, Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data (including lensing) from Planck and the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT), and Pantheon+ Type Ia Supernovae (SNe Ia). The…

items.title: Hecke modules associated to certain ternary lattices of half-discriminant $p^2$ and $4p^2$
items.summary: We consider Hecke modules of orthogonal modular forms attached to definite ternary lattices of half-discriminant $p^2$ with $p$ prime and $4p^2$ with $p$ an odd prime. Where possible, we prove explicit Jacquet-Langlands style correspondences with spaces of classical modular forms (in the spirit of Birch and Hein-Tornaria-Voight), and give conjectures for the remaining genera. This is done by applying sequences of Watson-style transformations that reduce the discriminant while preserving the adelic orthogonal group.

items.title: Extreme mass ratio inspirals from the Hills mechanism, The eccentricity distribution of Hills EMRIs in LISA
items.summary: Extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are promising sources for future space-based gravitational-wave detectors. We investigate EMRIs produced through the Hills mechanism, in which a stellar-mass black-hole binary (BBH) is tidally separated by a massive black hole (MBH), leaving one component bound to it. We present the first self-consistent modelling of this channel, combining an orbit-averaged Fokker-Planck treatment of the nuclear star cluster (NSC), three-body modelling of the binary-MBH encounter, Monte Carlo…

items.title: Existence of ergodic invariant measures for 3D Navier-Stokes eqs with superlinear noise
items.summary: We consider the Navier-Stokes equations in a smooth bounded domain $D\subset \mathbb R^3$. It has been proved in arXiv:2609.08284 that these equations have a unique solution - globally defined in time - when a superlinear noise is introduced and the initial velocity belongs to the space $V$ of divergence-free $H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^3)$-vector fields. Here we show that the same result holds when there is also an additive noise and a deterministic forcing term. Moreover, when the deterministic forcing term is…

items.title: Global Regular Solutions for One-Dimensional Degenerate Compressible Non-Resistive MHD Equations with Large Data and Far-Field Vacuum
items.summary: We consider the Cauchy problem on the real line for a one-dimensional transverse-field isentropic non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system with viscosity $μ(ρ)=αρ^δ$, $0<δ\leq1$, and vacuum at spatial infinity. The viscosity therefore vanishes precisely where the density vanishes. We establish two global large-data theorems, one for the sublinear range $0<δ<1$ and one for the linear case $δ=1$, in a nontrivial invariant class of magnetic fields. The class is described by the frozen-in flux $h=b/ρ$ and its mass…

items.title: The origin of amplitude chaos and strings
items.summary: We analytically study the peak statistics of an amplitude ensemble to identify the local mechanism responsible for peak repulsion. Our analytical approaches show that a smooth, nondegenerate ensemble of sufficiently differentiable amplitudes exhibits quartic nearest-neighbor repulsion, $p_{\rm nn}(S)\sim S^4$, where $S$ is the spacing between adjacent peaks. We verify this prediction numerically for the tree-level highly excited string scattering amplitudes. Interestingly, we find the quartic repulsion to be…

items.title: A 9-billion-year-old signal could help explain dark energy
items.summary: A Canadian radio telescope has detected the faint glow of hydrogen from billions of years ago using only its own observations, proving a long-awaited way to map the distant universe can actually work. CHIME can use this hydrogen signal to trace how matter is spread across space and measure how the universe has expanded over time, offering a powerful new way to investigate dark energy.

items.title: Non-resonant Flavoured leptogenesis with aligned two-Higgs doublet model and right-handed neutrinos
items.summary: We explore the possibility of non-resonant flavoured leptogenesis in the framework of the aligned two-Higgs doublet model augmented with two right-handed neutrinos. Considering the lightest heavy neutrino mass between 10 TeV-100 TeV, we calculate the baryon asymmetry of the universe by solving fully flavoured coupled Boltzmann equations and find that the observed baryon asymmetry can be successfully generated for lightest heavy-neutrino masses in this range without relying on resonant enhancement. We compute the…

items.title: The Population of Type~1 Active Galactic Nuclei in Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument. I. Profile-dependent Measurements of the Low-redshift Sample
items.summary: We present a spectral analysis of a large sample of low-redshift type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) selected from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1). For objects at $z\le0.9$, we perform spectral fitting and ML-assisted refinement, yielding 114,754 type 1 AGNs. We use two fitting schemes that differ only in the broad-line model: the broad Balmer components are fitted with either a Lorentzian function or a sum of Gaussians. The continuum and [O III] luminosity…

items.title: Open WDVV equations for non-commutative families of bounding cochains
items.summary: We derive the noncommutative open WDVV equations for the open Gromov-Witten superpotential introduced in joint work of the author and Solomon, extending the Solomon-Tukachinsky equations to noncommutative differential graded algebras. The resulting recursive formulas facilitate the computation of open Gromov-Witten invariants with multiple boundary point constraints for even-dimensional Lagrangians. We apply the open WDVV equations to compute all open Gromov-Witten invariants for the real loci of even-dimensional…

items.title: Boundedness of polarized log Calabi-Yau fibrations
items.summary: We investigate the boundedness problem for log Calabi-Yau fibrations whose bases and general fibers are bounded. We improve the results in arXiv:2504.05243 from birational boundedness to actual boundedness, which confirms a conjecture of Birkar and Hacon when the boundary coefficients belong to a fixed finite rational set. We also get a new proof for the birational boundedness result in arXiv:2504.05243 which is substantially more conceptual.

items.title: Stieltjes constants for Hurwitz-type L-series attached to periodic arithmetic functions
items.summary: We investigate generalized Stieltjes constants attached to Hurwitz-type Dirichlet series of the form $$ L(s, f, x)=\sum_{n \geq 0} \frac{f(n)}{(n+x)^s} $$ where $f$ is a periodic arithmetic function and $x\in\mathbb C\backslash\{0,-1,-2,\dots\}.$ We prove that these series admit meromorphic continuation to the whole complex plane, with at most a simple pole at $s=1$. We further derive functional equations satisfied by $L(s,f,x).$ Our main result gives an explicit formulas of the Stieltjes constants $γ_n(f, x)$…

items.title: Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane, with a proof formalized in Lean
items.summary: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to similarity. This settles Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane. Albouy and Kaloshin proved it for masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two. We follow their method. Infinitely many central configurations would give an algebraic curve of complex solutions. At the places at infinity of the curve the valuations of the mutual distances must balance. We…

items.title: The Order Mass Identity of Rooted Forests, with a Direct Proof of the Extended Aldous-Broder Theorem
items.summary: The Aldous-Broder algorithm constructs a spanning tree from the first-entrance edges of a covering random walk. Its distribution is known, but deriving it by summing over the orders in which a fixed tree can be discovered remains difficult. In this paper, we evaluate this sum by establishing an order-mass identity for rooted forests. For real matrices with zero row sums, the identity expresses the sum of order weights associated with each root as a principal cofactor of a matrix on the roots, under a…

items.title: Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a dominant paradigm for enhancing LLMs' reasoning capabilities. Yet long-horizon autoregressive rollouts introduce a fundamental limitation: local policy mismatch can compound into severe state distribution shift over trajectories. Existing LLM RL methods, such as GRPO and GSPO, control policy mismatch at the token or sequence level, but overlook this trajectory-induced shift, causing training instability and eventual collapse as the horizon grows. To close the state…

items.title: What Should SFT Learn? Conditional Information Gain for Generalizable Post-Training
items.summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) remains a widely used approach for post-training large language models, because fixed demonstrations can directly introduce desired reasoning strategies and behavioral patterns. Yet forcing a model to imitate externally provided trajectories may also interfere with behaviors already supported by pretraining, limiting generalization beyond the training distribution. Recent dynamic SFT methods mitigate this issue by reweighting token-level supervision according to model-side signals…

items.title: Markovian Random Words, a Gaussian Random Matrix Model and Beyond
items.summary: After centering and scaling, the length of the longest weakly increasing subsequence of a finite-state Markov random word converges to a Brownian last-passage functional with dependent components. We investigate when this functional, and more generally the limiting RSK Young-diagram shape, admits a Gaussian random-matrix representation. We introduce Hermitian Gaussian matrices with correlated diagonal entries and show that isotropy of the Brownian covariance on the trace-zero hyperplane yields such a…

items.title: Collaborative Learning and Reasoning over Model Slices
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) excel across diverse tasks, benefiting from knowledge priors, in-context reasoning, and test-time computation. Despite these strengths, single-model reasoning remains vulnerable to error propagation, as later steps depend on the model's earlier outputs, leaving reasoning blind spots difficult to independently reassess. To address this limitation, we develop \textit{collaborative learning}, encompassing the construction of heterogeneous collaborators and the learning of effective…

items.title: Direct detection constraints on EFT operators for inelastic dark matter
items.summary: We convert existing exclusion limits on the elastic spin-independent (SI) dark matter--proton cross sections into upper bounds on the event rate, subsequently applying them to constrain other effective operators for inelastic scattering of light dark matter in the GeV mass region. We focus on three representative scenarios including the isoscalar, proton-philic, and the proton-philic spin-dependent inelastic dark matter model, which are well-motivated in phenomenological studies of dark matter detection.

items.title: Collaborative Theory of Mind: Learning to Self-Revise by Anticipating User Responses
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong individual task performance, yet still struggle to collaborate with users over extended, multi-turn interactions, for example by attempting solutions before understanding the user's needs or by failing to revise mistaken assumptions after receiving feedback. We propose Collaborative Theory of Mind (CToM), a framework that addresses these challenges by explicitly training LLMs to anticipate user responses and to use those predictions to improve their own behavior…

items.title: On the Imaginary Part of $ζ'/ζ$
items.summary: We derive an explicit zero-side formula for the imaginary part of a smooth truncation of the logarithmic derivative of the Riemann zeta-function. The resulting kernel is the odd companion of the Fejér kernel in Montgomery's pair-correlation identity. Motivated by the recent breakthrough of Anthropic's Claude \cite{Claude26}, we also give an expository account of how the real-part identity can be turned into a matrix problem, overcoming the clustering obstruction for zeros off the critical line. Finally, we…

items.title: Compact Mean Curvature Flows from Non-Compact Initial Data
items.summary: We construct compact, embedded solutions to the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ that arise from various non-compact initial data and exist for a finite time.

items.title: Stability threshold of the Couette flow in 2D Navier-Stokes Boussinesq equations on $\mathbbT \times [-1, 1]$ and $\mathbbR \times [-1, 1]$
items.summary: In this paper, we study the transition threshold problem for the 2D Navier-Stokes Boussinesq equations around the Couette flow with a constant background temperature in two domains: $\mathbb{T} \times [-1, 1]$ and $\mathbb{R} \times [-1, 1]$. It was proved that if the sizes of initial perturbations of the vorticity and the temperature in Sobolev spaces are $ν^{\fr13}$ and $ν^{\fr56}$, respectively, then this system admits a globally stable solution. Besides, we derive the enhanced dissipation estimate for the…

items.title: The Complexity of Finding Additional Solutions
items.summary: We study the difficulty of finding a new solution when a list of distinct solutions is already supplied. For any fixed finite collection of list lengths, we can prescribe the additional-solution degrees while preserving a given $1$-paddable domain and first-solution degree. We also prove an exact compatibility condition for prescribing an arbitrary positive-list degree at the same time: it must dominate every prescribed fixed-level degree, and this condition suffices. All degrees use polynomial-time reductions…

items.title: AI and Chiral Fermions
items.summary: It turns out that yesterday there was another AI result coming out of OpenAI, quite different than the slopocalypse and of more interest to fundamental physics. Nathaniel Craig, a particle theorist now on a one-year visiting position at OpenAI, put … Continue reading →

items.title: Generic mean curvature flow has finitely many singularities
items.summary: We show that for a generic compact initial surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$, and any generic compact initial mean convex hypersurface in higher dimensions, the mean curvature flow encounters only finitely many singularities. This resolves the full generic Morse regularity conjectures of Ilmanen and Colding-Minicozzi-Pedersen in the above two cases. More generally, we show that if a mean curvature flow of a compact hypersurface has only multiplicity one spherical and cylindrical singularities, then after a small…

items.title: A Rigid Analytic Curve Can Have a Dense $p$-adic Orbit
items.summary: Let $\mathcal D$ be a product of Drinfeld upper half spaces and let $J$ be the corresponding product of projective linear groups acting on $\mathcal D$. We prove that if $Y$ is a reduced, quasi-compact separated strict $\mathbb C_p$-analytic space and $f: Y\to\mathcal D$ is analytic with $\dim Y<\dim\mathcal D$, then $J f(Y(\mathbb C_p))$ is closed and nowhere dense in $\mathcal D(\mathbb C_p)$. The quasi-compactness assumption is necessary even when the source is a strict rigid analytic curve, while a…

items.title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
items.summary: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a magnetic spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal has a maximum at $2k_c$ and, as expected from momentum conservation, has a sharp cutoff at that scale. We apply this analysis to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic…

items.title: Improving the lower bound on the Laughlin gap: An SDP search
items.summary: A recent preprint by OpenAI resolved the spherical fermionic Laughlin spectral-gap conjecture for the full $V_1$ interaction by a Fock-space inequality: $H_Q^2\ge γH_Q$ on the lowest-Landau-level Fock space for all large flux $Q$ and every $γ$ below $0.0461673\ldots$, so that the gap above the Laughlin state at filling $1/3$ is at least $1/25$. That proof, with its original constant, has also been formalized in Lean. We show that the same argument supports a much larger constant. Two sharper estimates, a…

items.title: Pointwise Hölder continuity of Lyapunov exponents of random matrix products
items.summary: We prove that if the first Lyapunov exponent of a compactly supported random matrix product is simple, then it is pointwise Hölder continuous for the Wasserstein--Hausdorff distance. By passing to exterior powers, we obtain pointwise Hölder continuity of the first $k$ exponents whenever they are simple.

items.title: Limit theorems for random matrix products with a simple top Lyapunov exponent
items.summary: We study products of independent, identically distributed random matrices with an exponential moment and a simple top Lyapunov exponent, without assuming irreducibility. Outside an exceptional invariant subspace called the equator, we establish contraction on average for a weighted projective distance and a spectral gap for the associated Markov operator. We obtain a central limit theorem, a Berry--Esseen bound, deviation estimates near the mean, and an almost sure invariance principle both for the growth of a…

items.title: A cyclotomic gluing construction for lattice sphere packings
items.summary: For a positive integer $d$, let $Δ_d^L$ denote the supremum of the densities of lattice sphere packings in $\mathbb R^d$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large $d$, $Δ_d^L \gg d^2\log\log d\,2^{-d}$. Abuya-Gargava-Zhao obtained the same bound along a sparse sequence of dimensions by combining Venkatesh's cyclotomic symmetries with Klartag's stochastic ellipsoid method. We introduce a multi-cyclotomic gluing construction that allows this argument to work in every sufficiently large dimension.

items.title: Dissipative Majorana Chain---Anomalies and Non-Invertible Symmetries
items.summary: We study symmetries and anomalies of dissipative Majorana chains described by Lindblad dynamics. Using the operator-state mapping, we represent the Lindbladian as a non-Hermitian operator on a doubled Hilbert space. In this formulation, the ket and bra contours admit strong fermion parities and strong translations, while their diagonal combinations define weak symmetries. For even and odd chain lengths, we diagnose anomalies by comparing symmetry algebras with and without weak fermion-parity defects. These…

items.title: Separating Field--Camp Alignment from Structural Balance in a Frustrated Random-Field Ising Model of Social Networks
items.summary: Frustrated Ising models of social networks mix ferromagnetic (agreement-seeking) and antiferromagnetic (antagonistic) couplings, and the antagonistic bonds are almost always placed independently at a fixed rate, yielding a +/-J spin glass. Real signed networks (Epinions, Slashdot, Wikipedia) instead show an excess of balanced triads, and perfectly balanced placement is gauge-equivalent to an unfrustrated ferromagnet. We compare three sign-placement conditions on a frustrated random-field Ising model of a…

items.title: GLSMs for non-polynomial deformations and generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau manifolds
items.summary: Gauged Linear Sigma Models (GLSMs) have long been a key tool in understanding Calabi-Yau compactifications of string theory. While descriptions of complete intersections of polynomial defining equations have long been understood in this context, a full treatment of non-polynomial complex structure deformations has been absent from the literature. Likewise, the somewhat more exotic generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau construction has resisted a GLSM description. In this paper we resolve both of these…

items.title: Proving the OSV conjecture with the gravitational path integral
items.summary: The OSV conjecture relates the helicity supertrace of black holes in $4d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity obtained through a Calabi--Yau compactification of Type IIA string theory to the modulus squared of the topological string partition function evaluated at the attractor point in moduli space for a given set of magnetic black hole charges and electric chemical potentials. We find Euclidean black hole saddles that compute this index to all orders in the 4d supergravity derivative expansion and calculate their…

items.title: Short-Range Vector Spin Glasses: Parisi Hierarchies and Real-Space Ultrametricity
items.summary: Replica symmetry breaking (RSB) is the organizing principle of mean-field spin-glass theory, yet whether a continuous Parisi hierarchy can arise in a genuinely short-range system in finite spatial dimension remains unresolved. Here we introduce a disordered model of $N$-component vector spins on a $D$-dimensional hypercubic lattice, with random matrix couplings on nearest-neighbor links and random tensor couplings on elementary plaquettes. In the large-$N$ limit, the model supports thermodynamically stable…

items.title: ACORN I. Massive Black Hole Seeding and Tidal Disruption Events from Star Clusters in Cosmological Simulations
items.summary: JWST has revealed massive star clusters at $z\gtrsim 6$, which provide promising environments for massive black hole (MBH) seed formation. We introduce a new MBH seeding model for cosmological simulations, physically motivated by runaway collisions in star clusters. Subgrid star clusters are generated according to the local ISM and evolved through stellar evolution and two-body relaxation. The masses of MBH seeds formed through runaway collisions are determined by the properties of their host clusters, including…

items.title: Endpoint Compactness and Finite-Energy Weak Solutions for the 2D Isothermal Compressible Navier-Stokes
items.summary: We prove global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the 2D isothermal compressible Navier--Stokes equations in bounded $C^2$ domains with no-slip boundary conditions. The initial data are arbitrary in the natural energy class, allowing vacuum and unbounded density. This resolves the isothermal endpoint $γ=1$ of the classical 2D finite-energy renormalized existence theory for power-law pressures. We develop a new endpoint compactness argument based on a truncation-independent integrable bound…

items.title: Local Constancy of the Betti Automorphic Category over the Moduli of Curves
items.summary: Nadler and Yun conjectured that the automorphic side of the Betti geometric Langlands correspondence forms a local system of categories over the moduli of curves. We prove this local constancy conjecture using purely microlocal methods, independent of the recently established Betti geometric Langlands conjecture. In particular, it follows that the Betti automorphic category depends only on the genus of the curve, verifying a conjecture of Ben-Zvi and Nadler.

items.title: Directed fractal percolation and non-Lipschitz variants
items.summary: While models of undirected and directed geometry in random i.i.d. disorder with rapidly decaying tails are expected to behave similarly and exhibit features of the Kardar--Parisi--Zhang universality class, the scenario when the background noise is fractal is expected to be significantly different. A canonical example of the latter is Liouville Quantum Gravity, where the planar Gaussian free field forms the fractal background. A toy model capturing some of the essential features is given by Mandelbrot's fractal…

items.title: Anomalous scaling limit of a Brownian particle in a log-correlated potential
items.summary: We study a Brownian particle in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\geq2$, with drift given by the gradient of a log-correlated Gaussian potential. At weak disorder, we prove convergence to a scaling limit whose law is singular with respect to Brownian motion and whose invariant measure is given by Gaussian multiplicative chaos. The proof uses a renormalization group induction: at each scale, the elliptic operator is well approximated by a Laplacian with effective diffusivity decaying as a power of scale. We compute this exponent…

items.title: Opening the Black Box: What Neural Networks Learn from Pulsar Timing Array Data
items.summary: In recent years, simulation-based inference (SBI) methods have been proposed to address several data-analysis challenges faced by existing and planned gravitational-wave experiments. For example, SBI classification has recently been shown to significantly improve the prospects for detecting anisotropies in pulsar timing array (PTA) data. In this work, we use a simple toy model of a PTA to provide a more pedagogical explanation of how, and under which circumstances, SBI-based detection can improve on classical…

items.title: Invariant sets and spectral rigidity of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms
items.summary: We solve a well-known question of Polterovich from 2002 regarding the rigidity of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms in Hofer's metric in dimension two: every non-trivial Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a surface of genus at least one has all positive iterations separated from the identity in Hofer's metric. In higher dimensions, we make progress on the case of autonomous Hamiltonian flows: we prove Hofer non-recurrence for symplectically hyperbolic manifolds, and completely characterize Hofer recurrence for functions of…

items.title: Negatively Curved Minimal Surfaces in the Round Four-Sphere
items.summary: We construct smooth closed embedded minimal surfaces with everywhere negative Gaussian curvature in the unit round four-sphere. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $m$, our construction gives a minimal surface $Σ_m$ of genus $m^2+1$ such that $\operatorname{Area}(Σ_m)\to 4π^2$ as $m\to+\infty$. This result yields a complete solution to Problem 101 in Yau's 1982 list of open problems.

items.title: Improved zero-free half-planes for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis
items.summary: Recently, a uniform $\frac{7}{8}$ zero-free half-plane for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and its transfer to Dirichlet $L$-functions was given by OpenAI in [Ope26a]. In its proof, there are several parameters $b=\frac{1}{8}, \ell=\frac{1}{6}$, and $κ$. In this paper, via varying $b$, $\ell$, and $κ$, following the same strategy, we slightly improve the bound $\frac{7}{8}=0.875$ to \[ B_{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{18ξ_{\mathrm{new}}+7}{18ξ_{\mathrm{new}}+9} =0.874957019420098946\ldots, \]…

items.title: On Igusa's conjectures for weighted homogeneous polynomials with isolated singularities
items.summary: In 1991, Denef introduced an explicit formula for Igusa's local zeta functions in terms of embedded resolutions of singularities over $p$-adic fields with good reduction. In this paper, by slightly generalizing the $p$-adic McKay correspondence given by the second author in 2017, we extend Denef's result to the setting of $\mathbb{Q}$-embedded resolutions of singularities. Consequently, the strong monodromy conjecture with respect to Igusa's local zeta functions holds for weighted homogeneous polynomials with…

items.title: Hierarchical Melnikov Realization: Logarithmic Factor Improvement to Hilbert Number Lower Bounds
items.summary: The second part of Hilbert's 16th problem is one of the most fundamental open problems in the qualitative theory of ordinary differential equations and dynamical systems. A central unresolved question is whether the Hilbert number $H(d)$ is finite for arbitrary polynomial degree $d$. (A very recent manuscript from OpenAI asserts the finiteness of $H(d)$; see the remark at the end of this paper.) In the absence of a general upper bound theory, most existing work constructs explicit perturbed polynomial systems to…

items.title: Verification with Transfer: Exact Information Frontiers and Their Price in Calls
items.summary: A verifier that accepts or rejects whole answers reveals little: under a flat prior over $k$-bit answers, zero error needs $2^k-1$ verifications. The usual remedy is to solve related source tasks, either all first, as a curriculum does, or interleaved with verification. We price this remedy in information and in calls. With an exact verifier, the least causal information that any interleaving of source calls and $n$ verifications needs to succeed with probability $s$ is a list rate-distortion function, attained…

items.title: Evidence for Normal Neutrino Ordering with Combined Atmospheric Neutrino Experiments
items.summary: We present a combined analysis of the latest publicly available atmospheric neutrino data from Super-Kamiokande including all data-taking stages previous to the gadolinium phase, IceCube-DeepCore, and the six-detection-unit configuration of KM3NeT/ORCA. Our fit uses all event samples simultaneously and treats the systematic uncertainties shared among experiments as fully correlated, while detector-response uncertainties are modeled independently for each experiment. The combined data constrain the atmospheric…

items.title: Topological inequalities for conic-line arrangements with some prescribed singularities
items.summary: We study arrangements of conics and lines in the complex projective plane from the viewpoint of 4-manifolds. We introduce combinatorial conic-line arrangements, the conic-line counterpart of rank-3 matroids, together with their topological and smooth realisations, and we ask which restrictions on a complex arrangement survive when its components are replaced by locally-flat spheres in the same homology classes with the same local singularity models. For an ADE combinatorial conic-line arrangement of even total…

items.title: Geometric families of multiple elliptic Gamma functions and arithmetic applications, III
items.summary: This is the third paper in a series where we study arithmetic applications of the higher elliptic Gamma functions. In the first two articles in this series, we defined geometric families of these functions and proved that they satisfy coboundary and cocycle relations under the action of special linear groups and associated congruence subgroups. The main purpose of the present paper is to present a construction of conjectural higher elliptic units above number fields with exactly one complex place as special…

items.title: Learning to Plan by Looking Back: Hindsight Hierarchies for Training Reasoning Models
items.summary: We introduce a self-improvement loop for reasoning models based on the following observation: Even when the difficulty of a problem exceeds the model's current solving abilities, an additionally supplied solution might enable the model to extract useful solution ideas in hindsight. We operationalize this by jointly training the same model to exhibit the following three capabilities: predicting solution ideas from problems alone, reverse-engineering ideas from problems and known solutions, and solving problems…

items.title: Lower bounds for Ramsey numbers: $\mathrmR(6,8)\ge 135$ and $\mathrmR(8,10)\ge 345$
items.summary: We prove the lower bounds $\mathrm{R}(6,8)\ge 135$ and $\mathrm{R}(8,10)\ge 345$, improving the bounds 134 and 343 listed in the April 2026 revision of Radziszowski's dynamic survey. We give explicit red/blue colorings of $K_{134}$ with no red $K_6$ or blue $K_8$, and of $K_{344}$ with no red $K_8$ or blue $K_{10}$, and verify them with two independently written exhaustive clique checkers. Starting from published colorings, we find these witnesses by adding vertices and repairing the resulting monochromatic…

items.title: Universal Textual Teaching for LLMs
items.summary: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from stronger Teacher models to weaker Student models, but most methods require training the Student parameters, thereby binding the distilled knowledge to a specific architecture and checkpoint. This implicit representation is difficult to interpret or reuse across models and limits KD for API-only or costly-to-train models. This paper studies knowledge transfer for large language models (LLMs). We introduce Universal Textual Teaching (UTT), a parameter-update-free…

items.title: An updated model of neutrino emission from proto-neutron stars
items.summary: We present an improved parametric model for neutrino emission from core-collapse supernovae that directly connects neutrino luminosity and average energy to stellar properties during emission. Our model incorporates two critical physical processes: convection within the proto-neutron star and the evolution of the neutrinosphere radius during the early emission phase. Using simulated datasets of supernova neutrino events in the Super-Kamiokande detector, we assess the sensitivity to astrophysical properties in the…

items.title: Natural Language to First-Order Logic LLM-based Autoformalization
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have renewed interest in autoformalization. Yet, when First-Order Logic (FOL) is considered as the target formalism, the field still lacks a unified task formulation and a systematic survey. This paper addresses this gap: we first provide a principled definition for the FOL-autoformalization task by distinguishing Ontology Extraction from Logical Translation, showing how their conflation obscures (cross-study) evaluation; we review existing datasets, evaluation metrics, and LLM-based…

items.title: Uniform non-vanishing of prime quadratic twists of standard and symmetric square $L$-functions
items.summary: Let $S_k$ be the space of cusp forms of weight $k$ for ${\rm SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$, with $\dim S_k\geq1$, and let $χ_p=\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ for odd primes $p$. For fixed $s$ with ${\rm Re}(s)>(k+1)/2$, we prove that the proportion of primes $p\leq X$ satisfying $L(h,χ_p,s)=0$ tends to zero as $X\to\infty$, uniformly over nonzero $h\in S_k$. We also prove an analogous statement for nontrivial linear combinations of twisted symmetric square $L$-values of the normalized Hecke eigenforms when ${\rm Re}(s)>k$…

items.title: Temporal chirality in Floquet photonic media
items.summary: We reveal temporal chirality in time-modulated photonic media: reversing the orientation of a closed loop traced by the complex permittivity can leave the Floquet spectrum unchanged while strongly modifying the directional scattering response under the same excitation. This behavior is linked to two symmetry constraints on the evolution operator, namely pseudo-Hermiticity and pseudo-unitarity. We prove the general occurrence of temporal chirality based on a complex Bogoliubov parametrization of the scattering…

items.title: Rigidity of Kähler-Ricci Solitons with Constant Scalar Curvature
items.summary: Let $(M^{2m},g,f,J)$ be a complete nonsteady gradient Kähler-Ricci soliton satisfying $\mathrm{Ric}+\nabla^2 f=λg$, $λ\neq 0$. We prove that constant scalar curvature forces the soliton to be rigid. More precisely, the universal cover splits holomorphically and isometrically as $N^{2k}\times\mathbb{C}^{m-k}$, where $N^{2k}$ is Kähler-Einstein with $\mathrm{Ric}_{g_N}=λg_N$. In the shrinking case the quotient is trivial; in the normalization $λ=1/2$ one has $R\equiv k$. The Kähler result rests on a Riemannian…

items.title: On Calabi-Yau varieties that are linear sections of Grassmannians of lines
items.summary: In this paper we consider the $n-3$ dimensional linear section $X_Π$ of the Grassmannian $\mathbb G(1,n)$ of lines in $\mathbb P^n$ with a general linear space $Π$ of codimension $n+1$, with $n=2k+1$ odd and $n\geq 5$, that is a Calabi-Yau variety. Related to $X_Π$ there is a degree $k+1$ Pfaffian hypersurface $\mathcal C_Π$ that is the intersection of the dual of $\mathbb G(1,n)$ with $Π^\perp$. We prove that $\mathcal C_Π$ is rational and we provide a birational parametrization of it. Moreover we study in some…

items.title: Fluid deformable surfaces with variable thickness - a Surface Shallow-Water-Helfrich model
items.summary: Epithelial tissues play a fundamental role in morphogenesis. Mechanically they can be viewed as thin soft materials exhibiting a solid-fluid duality. The Surface Navier-Stokes-Helfrich model accounts for these properties by combining bending and surface hydrodynamics. In order to account for varying cell thickness we incorporate a thickness field in the spirit of a shallow-water equation, but defined on the (self-)evolving surface. This replaces the inextensibility constraint of the two-dimensional fluid and with…

items.title: Coarse ellipticity and De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory in the optimal range
items.summary: We extend the theory of De Giorgi-Nash-Moser to elliptic equations with symmetric coefficients $\mathbf{a}(x)$ which are possibly degenerate and unbounded but satisfy a coarse ellipticity condition. We prove local upper bounds for weak subsolutions, a weak Harnack inequality for nonnegative supersolutions, and a Harnack inequality for nonnegative solutions. The coarse ellipticity hypothesis requires spatial moments of coarse-grained matrices, suitably discounted and summed across scales, to be finite. In…

items.title: Electromagnetic isospin breaking in hadronic vacuum polarization within a VMD model
items.summary: One of the challenging components of modern lattice-QCD computations of the leading hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $(g-2)_μ$ is the isospin-breaking correction due to electromagnetism. Dominated by long distances, this correction suffers from severe signal-to-noise issues and finite-volume effects. To provide infinite-volume benchmarks for various quark-level Wick contractions, we estimate their sizes phenomenologically at the physical point, using a previously developed…

items.title: The rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over F2 is 23
items.summary: The rank of the tensor of $3\times 3$ matrix multiplication over the field with two elements is at most $23$ by Laderman's algorithm, and Rudich and Rousseau recently proved that it is at least $22$. We prove that it equals $23$. Hence Laderman's algorithm uses the fewest multiplications among all bilinear algorithms over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and among all bilinear algorithms with integer coefficients. The proof uses the substitution method in the form developed by D'Ambrosio, Wang and Yang et al., which bounds the…

items.title: Loyalty of the affine line in motivic homotopy theory
items.summary: We show that integers act invertibly on a derived scheme $S$ if and only if they act invertibly on the reduced motivic suspension spectrum of the affine line in $\mathrm{MS}_S$. As a consequence, over regular locally noetherian schemes and derived schemes on which some nonzero integer acts as zero, the motivic sphere spectrum is $\mathbf{A}^1$-invariant after inverting primes that are not invertible in the base scheme. In particular, over regular locally noetherian $\mathbf{Q}$-schemes, the motivic sphere…

items.title: Minimally modified Frampton--Glashow--Yanagida ansatz and its leptogenesis consequences: in light of recent JUNO's result
items.summary: Motivated by the recent JUNO indication favoring normal neutrino mass ordering, we study two realizations of the minimally modified Frampton--Glashow--Yanagida (MMFGY) framework in the minimal type-I seesaw with two right-handed neutrinos. Both retain one exact Yukawa texture zero, supplemented by either a single physical CP-violating phase or a remnant CP symmetry. The explicit-CP realization yields twelve high-energy Yukawa configurations that reduce to three low-energy classes, with correlated CP phases and…

items.title: Extremal black hole mimickers: geometry, stability, and long-delay signal trains
items.summary: We present a spacetime that serves as a horizonless mimicker of extremal black holes. Unlike previously studied mimickers of black holes with non-degenerate horizons, whose geometries are of the wormhole type and consist of two asymptotically flat regions connected by a very long throat, the mimicker of an extremal black hole possesses a single asymptotically flat region at one end and an infinitely long throat at the other. In the throat region, the spacetime approaches the direct-product geometry $M_{1,1}…

items.title: Einstein Probe reveals a hidden phase of neutron star collisions
items.summary: Einstein Probe revealed nearly 10 minutes of soft X-ray activity following a short gamma-ray burst, exposing a phase of neutron star mergers that previous missions may have missed. The prolonged emission could have been powered by a newly formed magnetar and may provide a valuable new counterpart to gravitational-wave signals.

items.title: Where to Adapt Matters: Layer-Selective Fine-Tuning for Capability Retention
items.summary: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) enables large language models (LLMs) to adapt to specialized tasks, but often at the cost of degrading general capabilities acquired during pretraining. Existing approaches primarily mitigate this trade-off through data replay or regularization, relying on additional data or explicit optimization constraints. items.title: Holographic dark energy from generalized entropies and extended infrared cut-offs
items.summary: We study holographic dark energy models constructed from generalized entropy functionals and local infrared cut-offs. Three entropies (Barrow and the three and five-parameter generalized entropies) are each combined with the Granda-Oliveros (GO) cut-off and two extensions, one adding a $γH^{-2}$ term and one a $γ\ddot{H}/H$ term, the latter raising the dark-energy evolution equation to second order. items.title: NanoProof: Open and Efficient Automated Theorem Proving in Lean 4
items.summary: We introduce NanoProof, to our knowledge the first factorized execution-guided theorem prover in Lean 4 whose training data, extraction tooling, training pipeline, and weights are all released, making it end-to-end reproducible using open-source resources. To this end, we build and release a dataset of structured proof trees, as well as a tool for programmatic interaction and data extraction within the Lean 4 formal verifier. items.title: An improved lower bound for the minimum-autocorrelation constant
items.summary: We construct nonnegative bounded compactly supported functions on the real line that give the lower bound $\mathcal{A}\ge 0.4103779774321214877852987\ldots$ for the minimum-autocorrelation constant. This improves the explicitly certified bound $2378625/5958277=0.39921356\ldots$ reported by Russell. items.title: Fed-GRPO: Reward-Signal-Driven Federated Group Relative Policy Optimization
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong reasoning capabilities when fine-tuned with reinforcement learning (RL), particularly through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). However, existing GRPO methods assume centralized access to training data, which may not hold in practice due to privacy or regulatory constraints. To this end, we propose Fed-GRPO, a federated GRPO training framework that addresses these privacy constraints by enabling collaborative reasoning training without sharing raw data…

items.title: Quantum Gravity in Asymptotically Flat Spacetimes from Unstable D-Branes
items.summary: We present a non-perturbative formulation of quantum gravity in asymptotically flat spacetimes using Witten's cubic open string field theory (OSFT) on unstable D-branes. Given that the massless spin-2 sector of the closed string spectrum inherently encodes the degrees of freedom of quantum gravity, we establish this connection by mapping on-shell closed string excitations directly to gauge-invariant operators in OSFT, realizing a concrete flat-space analogue of the AdS/CFT correspondence. items.title: Net drag reduction in turbulent pipe flow by airfoil-section grids concentrated near the wall
items.summary: The frictional drag of turbulent pipe flow is responsible for enormous energy consumption in water and natural gas distribution systems. Flow straighteners can reduce this drag by suppressing turbulence, but they generally induce a pressure loss that exceeds the reduction; similarly, large-eddy breakup devices installed in pipes have not achieved a net drag reduction. In this study, a grid of NACA0006 airfoils was adopted as a flow straightener to suppress the pressure loss, and its net drag reduction was…

items.title: Spanning Even Linear Forests with Isolated Edges Share the Anti-Ramsey Numbers of Perfect Matchings
items.summary: The anti-Ramsey number $AR(n,F)$ is the maximum number of colors in an edge-coloring of the complete graph $K_n$ containing no rainbow copy of $F$. I prove that every spanning linear forest on an even number $n\ge6$ of vertices whose components have even orders and which has an isolated edge has the same anti-Ramsey number as a perfect matching on $n$ vertices. The orders of the longer path components may be different.

items.title: Automorphic symbols and automorphic \emphL-values of GL(2) over imaginary quadratic fields
items.summary: We study non-vanishing modulo primes of critical values of $L$-functions over imaginary quadratic fields twisted by Coates--Wiles characters. items.title: Local Existence and Uniqueness for the 3D Compressible Navier-Stokes/Cahn-Hilliard System with Vacuum
items.summary: We establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes/Cahn-Hilliard system in a bounded smooth domain in $\mathbb R^3$, allowing the initial density to vanish. items.title: Implications of tachyonic phase transition in classically scale invariant general $U(1)_{X}$ models
items.summary: We investigate the complementarity between collider searches and gravitational-wave (GW) observations in the classically scale-invariant general $U(1)_X$ extension of the Standard Model. items.title: Finite Symplectic Automorphisms of Hyperkähler Manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$-Type Act Trivially on Discriminant Groups
items.summary: We give an alternative proof of Mongardi's result that every finite group of symplectic automorphisms of a hyperkähler manifold of $K3^{[n]}$-type acts trivially on the discriminant groups of its second cohomology lattice and its coinvariant lattice. The proof combines sphere-packing bounds, Vinberg's reflection chambers and structure results on even $2$-elementary lattices.

items.title: Braidings of Self-Equivalences and Bordism
items.summary: Let $M$ be a closed, smooth or topological $n$-manifold, with $n \geq 4$. We construct a homotopy highly cartesian square relating the space ${\mathcal E}(M (\ell))$ of homotopy self-equivalences of $M$ (in a suitable range) over the Postnikov $\ell$-sections of its stable normal microbundle, and an $(\infty + n)$-fold loop space representing an associated (normal) bordism theory. items.title: Cova-PINN: Cross-Domain Conservation Physics-Informed Neural Network for Fluid-Solid Conjugate Heat Transfer in Complex Geometries
items.summary: Multi-domain physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) flexibly model medium-specific representations to solve fluid--solid conjugate heat transfer (CHT). However, standard multi-domain PINNs enforce governing equations and interface conditions on separately sampled domain supports, which can yield plausible temperature fields but inaccurate end-to-end energy transfer and outlet temperatures. items.title: Revisiting self-interacting dark matter with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation observations
items.summary: We revisit self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), originally proposed to resolve small-scale CDM problems and drive late-time cosmic acceleration. Using latest DESI BAO, Pantheon+/DESY5 type Ia supernova, and cosmic chronometer Hubble data, we constrain three representative SIDM scenarios including creation and annihilation. items.title: Condensed Whitehead Problem
items.summary: The Whitehead problem, which asks whether every abelian group $A$ satisfying $\mathrm{Ext}^1(A,\mathbb{Z}) = 0$ is free, is independent of ZFC. However, this problem has an analogue in condensed mathematics that can be answered affirmatively. In this note, we give a new proof that an abelian group $ A $ of size $κ$ is free if and only if $\underline{\mathrm{Ext}}^1(\underline{A}, \underline{\mathbb{Z}})(S_κ) = 0$, where $ S_κ$ is the Stone space of the Boolean completion of $\operatorname{Add}(ω,κ)$.

items.title: Almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum
items.summary: Haemers' conjecture for the generalized spectrum asserts that almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum, that is, for almost all graphs $G$, every graph with the same spectrum as $G$ whose complement has the same spectrum as the complement of $G$ is isomorphic to $G$. items.title: Riemann functions for almost primes and their counting errors
items.summary: The real-axis jump of the prime-zeta function gives an integral form of Gram's series for Riemann's $R$-function. items.title: Reading Altermagnetic Domains with Photon Drag
items.summary: Finite photon momentum allows second-order photocurrents in centrosymmetric space groups, where the conventional bulk photovoltaic effect is forbidden. Here we study the photon-drag response of altermagnets and show that its angular dependence reveals both the symmetry of the magnetic order and the Néel domain of the sample. items.title: Stochastic Teacher Intervention for Agentic On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) efficiently transfers capabilities from a stronger teacher to a student language model through dense token-level supervision on student-generated rollouts and has shown promise on complex tasks such as mathematical reasoning. items.title: Smoothing Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and del Pezzo cone points
items.summary: We give a necessary and sufficient homological criterion for smoothing projective Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and anticanonical cones over smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degrees five, six and seven, or over a smooth quadric surface. items.title: K-moduli wall crossing for quasimaps to a projective variety
items.summary: We develop a modular wall crossing theory for quasimaps to a projective variety, allowing independent variation of the boundary coefficients and the quasimap weight. Building on the K-stability of quasimaps introduced by Hashizume and the first author, we construct projective moduli spaces in the stable, Calabi--Yau, and log Fano regimes, together with wall crossing morphisms. items.title: VICO: Visual Environments Co-Evolving for Vision-Language Model Reasoning
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become a standard recipe for post-training vision-language models (VLMs), but it typically assumes a static training environment. As the actor improves, fixed tasks drift out of its learning frontier: many become trivial, others remain unsolvable; and the learning signal collapses. items.title: Reconstruction of Black Hole Islands from Hawking Radiation via the Algebraic Petz Map
items.summary: The island proposal guarantees a unitary Page curve for evaporating black holes, implying that operators deep behind the horizon must be fully reconstructable from asymptotic Hawking radiation. However, because the interior is causally disconnected and highly dynamical, standard entanglement wedge reconstruction methods, relying on global isometries or continuous modular flow, fail to provide this mapping. items.title: Gauging Modulated Symmetries: Bond Algebras, Higher-Form Symmetries, and Symmetry-Enriched Topological Order
items.summary: We develop a constructive framework for characterizing modulated symmetries and their gauging in $d$-dimensional lattice systems. items.title: The hidden sunrise in the energy-energy correlator
items.summary: The energy-energy correlator (EEC) is one of a handful of collider observables that can be computed analytically to high orders. As an energy-weighted cross-section, it exposes features of quantum field theory that scattering amplitudes do not, and it can be compared directly to data. As with scattering amplitudes, the analytic expressions require special functions beyond polylogarithms. items.title: A Texture of Leptons for the Koide and Alikhanov relations
items.summary: Koide and Alikhanov proposed intriguing empirical relations among charged-lepton masses and neutrino mass splittings, respectively. We present mass-matrix textures that realise these relations and can jointly account for the observed lepton mixing angles, while yielding predictive correlations among them and the neutrino CP phases.

We search for a contribution in the high-latitude sky and in the region of the Galactic Stellar Halo that would be beyond known astrophysical emissions, i.e., the galactic diffuse emission, the isotropic mostly extragalactic gamma-ray background, the Fermi Bubbles, Loop I, the contribution from the Galactic Center Excess, and the known point and extended gamma-ray sources detected by the Fermi-LAT Collaboration. items.title: General Spin-1 Dynamics During Inflation: Microcausality Constraints and Cosmological Collider Signals
items.summary: We construct the general theory of a spin-1 field propagating on an inflationary background consistent with scale invariance, rotations, Bunch-Davies conditions and microcausality. Our Boostless Proca theory generalises the usual massive Proca theory to a Lagrangian with 5 free parameters: 4 corresponding to parity-even terms and a single parity-odd term. items.title: Neutrino flavor conversion alters the lepton-emission self-sustained asymmetry in core-collapse supernovae
items.summary: We solve the neutrino equations of motion in a half annulus, accounting for two spatial dimensions. At any location in the annulus, the neutrino momentum is characterized by a polar-angle distribution, two effective azimuthal angles, and an energy distribution. items.title: Interpretation of Nanohertz Gravitational Waves via Cosmic Strings in Post-BBN Matter and Kination Domination
items.summary: Recent pulsar timing array (PTA) observations have reported evidence for a common low frequency signal consistent with a stochastic gravitational wave background. items.title: Primordial black holes as a natural consequence of scale-invariance
items.summary: We show that a scale-invariant $U(1)$ gauge theory can naturally realize large curvature perturbations around the end of thermal inflation, seeding the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). items.summary: Hawking amplitudes provide a new way of determining the Hawking spectrum of black holes, using on-shell techniques borrowed from the literature on scattering amplitudes. items.summary: We argue that the scattering amplitude of a single minus helicity gluon with arbitrarily many positive helicity gluons is topological. items.summary: Modern language models undergo reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) on top of already-trained checkpoints. A key promise of RLVR is the discovery of new reasoning strategies. In principle, a model can sample novel ideas absent from its prior training data. items.title: The circle packing and Riemann uniformization embedding of the tree-weighted planar maps converges to Liouville quantum gravity
items.summary: We prove that in the disk, sphere, whole-plane topology, spanning tree weighted planar maps converge to $\sqrt{2}$-Liouville quantum gravity disk, sphere or cone under circle packing and Riemann uniformization embedding as the number of faces of the map goes to infinity. items.summary: Suppose $M$ is a planar map with a macroscopic boundary decorated by a spanning tree $T$, such that $(M,T)$ has been sampled from the critical Boltzman measure. items.title: Sharp dynamical isoperimetric principle for mean curvature flow

items.title: Simultaneous non-vanishing of twists of $\mathrmGL_3$ and $\mathrmGL_1$ $L$-functions

items.title: The NANOGrav 15 yr Dataset: Modified Functional Forms for Profile-Evolution Time Delays in Pulsar Timing Models

items.summary: Min-Plus Convolution is a central problem in fine-grained complexity, and the associated Min-Plus Convolution Hypothesis forms the basis for a wide range of conditional lower bounds for fundamental problems. items.summary: It is well known that the compressible Euler equations with planar shock initial data may admit infinitely many entropy weak solutions, as shown by Chiodaroli, De Lellis and Kreml [Comm. items.summary: We show that if the 3SUM problem on integer-valued inputs can be solved in truly subquadratic time, then it can also be solved in truly subquadratic time on real-valued inputs.
